5361.title: Journeys viewer
5361.content: Draw every journey (user-scenario) and workshop (workshop) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser a layer declares for this Tool, <locale>/<instance>/<id>/: an index of all journeys, grouped by layer (each a sub-graph page), each parent’s parts nested under it in its order with optional and repeating parts marked (an older file’s partOf children after them, ordered along follows), and a plain DAK user scenario with no steps listed as one; one page per journey, its parts in order and the journeys it is a part of, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step, linked to the journey it includes, with its BPMN drawing (the step’s flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks, the DAK assets it uses (data sets, decision tables and indicators, linked into the IG) and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets; and each device screen (device-screen) that shows a step a workshop presents, drawn as a static device mock (phone, tablet, scanner, desktop, kiosk) with its owner beside it, in the workshop’s Device Demo, linked both ways with the walkthrough. A persona’s picture (meta.persona.avatar) is drawn wherever the persona appears. Layers below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too. |   |   | . | Tool | journeys-viewer | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/journeys-viewer/journeys-viewer.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

Package, release, distribute, and retrieve Knowledge Graphs using npm tooling and tarballs: declare package.json as an authored pre-packaging asset in the Knowledge Graph, build .tgz packages via bun pm pack, record publications as folio-binary-release/v1 state documents hosted on GitHub binary releases, and retrieve remote Knowledge Graphs using npm install for both unhydrated source graph and hydrated materialized graph views. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or --out could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. --markdown and --warn always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither. | string · Markdown text. 5436.title: Skills it satisfies
5436.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. merge-conflict-patterns . Merge the base branch in and resolve, without a person, only the conflicts a DECLARED pattern covers — generated files, generated README regions, QA sidecars — then prove the result with the gate set. Refuses the whole merge when any conflict is authored or undeclared. Use for “merge main”, “resolve the conflicts”, “the PR is conflicted again”, “auto-resolve”, and when adding a pattern for a new kind of churn. Also governs what a merge steward does with a merge-train member it had to refuse: one deduplicated work item under the PR’s own epic, a hand-back to the owning session with a fail condition, one dispatched agent when nobody owns it, one PR comment, and the close. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/merge-conflict-patterns.md. Also satisfied by: merge-leftover, merge-train. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/merge-conflict-patterns/{input,output}.schema.json). coordinate . Coordinate work across multiple in-flight Claude PRs working toward a shared goal. Post intent + asks on related PRs, identify cherry-pickable work, respond to code-review comments on your own PR, periodically triage sibling PR activity (new comments, CI status, new commits), watch main + newly created branches/PRs, escalate inconsistent findings to the author, and keep a coordination ledger up to date. Source: cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/coordinate.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/coordinate/{input,output}.schema.json).

5534.title: Collect candidate translations from open engines
5534.content: Ask one or more open, self-hosted machine translators — OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP Marian models, CC-BY 4.0, run locally) and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate (AGPL, Argos models) — for CANDIDATE translations of each empty or fuzzy string, so no freemium API quota is involved. Candidates are appended to <locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json (translation-candidates/v1) for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page; a candidate whose placeholders or markup do not round-trip is not recorded. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an EMPTY msgstr gets the first good candidate, marked #, fuzzy; a non-empty msgstr is never overwritten. The translation node records the source (generatedBy: "machine", model, time); official is never set, and a candidate is never a verdict. A catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or whose node is official, gets candidates but no fill. |   |   | . | Tool | translation-candidates | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness/cat-harness.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness | . | source | cat-harness/tools/translation-candidates/translation-candidates.json | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

5568.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-adjudication . A person’s verdict on a machine translation, carried from the translation review page to the record: the reviewer accepts a catalogue, or flags a mistranslation and picks a candidate or writes their own text; the verdict is filed as a translation-adjudication/v1 issue; a workflow checks the author and the catalogue’s hash, writes the records and opens a PR; a maintainer merges it. 5625.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. translation-candidate-source . The one interface every candidate-translation engine meets: for a layer’s catalogues, append candidate translations per string to the translation-candidates/v1 sidecar, each carrying its source, and seed an empty msgstr with the first candidate marked fuzzy. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, the poSources fallback resolution chain, and translating into several locales as a team: one extraction, a PR per locale to main, FHIR terms as CodeSystem supplements, the untainted round trip as run, and the per-locale QA report. Source: cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/translation-manager.md. Also satisfied by: translation-extract, translation-inject, translation-roundtrip-record, translation-signoff, translation-status, translation-validate. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/translation-manager/{input,output}.schema.json).

Pre-declaration corpus check. Before declaring any item “open”, “gap”, “TODO”, “open problem”, “pending derivation” — or asserting in chat that something is unresolved in the corpus — run the four-path grep checklist. A source file’s ## Status note lags the corpus by weeks; the corpus is the source of truth. An item is open only after all four paths come back empty (modulo the originating file itself). 5725.title: Tools — cat-harness
5725.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 184Tool nodes 77skills satisfied 154invoked as a shell command 29reachable over MCP

5726.content: Run a declared BPMN process as an instance: workflow_start opens one for a subject, workflow_next reports what is enabled, workflow_complete records a step or answers a decision (a DMN-computed one from facts) and REFUSES a step that is not enabled. State is committed under the work plan, so which edge was taken is a record, not a memory. |   |   | . | Tool | bpmn-engine | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness-tools/tools/bpmn-engine.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/cat-harness-tools/cat-harness-tools.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | cat-harness-tools | . | source | cat-harness-tools/tools/bpmn-engine/bpmn-engine.ts | . | invoked | inProcess mcp | . | qa | qa-reports | .

5727.title: Skills it satisfies
5727.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. process-state . Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. Read before completing a workflow step, and whenever something unexpected interrupts one. Covers what to do about notes and stickies you re-anchored while off-process, which leave no trace in the artefact. Source: cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/process-state.md. Also satisfied by: workflow-complete, workflow-gate, workflow-list, workflow-next, workflow-start. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/process-state/{input,output}.schema.json).

5740.title: Tools — cat-harness-tools
5740.content: The Tool nodes cat-harness-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 1Tool nodes 1skills satisfied 0invoked as a shell command 1reachable over MCP

5760.title: Spreadsheet tabular metadata
5760.content: Read a workbook into a folio-tabular-csvw/v1 record, one CSVW table per rectangular block of cells. Blocks are split on empty rows, then on empty columns, so several tables on one sheet are found, each anchored at its real top-left cell (fac:anchor: sheet, A1 cell, row, column). Dates are read through the number formats in styles.xml, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with node:zlib and SpreadsheetML with fast-xml-parser. 5784.title: ArchiMate model from the glossary
5784.content: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance’s folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term’s prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. 5800.title: Figure coverage and computability
5800.content: For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Exits non-zero when any declared figure is missing; --require-computable also fails on pictures, linked or not. |   |   | . | Tool | figure-coverage | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/figure-coverage.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/figure-coverage/figure-coverage.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

5801.title: Skills it satisfies
5801.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. figure-rebuild . Turn a figure into a computable diagram: every figure of a source publication when a folio is built from its L1 entry, and any hand-drawn figure in a folio, an IG or a demonstrator that is redrawn from a source. Every declared figure gets a block, and each one is rebuilt in the form its type calls for: an ArchiMate view, BPMN, DMN, a FHIR logical model, or an SVG generated from data, always from one schema-backed source. The PDF crop stays beside the rebuild as the cited source, and the rebuild keeps the original’s layout. The figure-coverage check counts what is missing and what is still only a picture. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/ingestion/figure-rebuild.md. Also satisfied by: diig-phases-svg, smart-approach-svg. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/figure-rebuild/{input,output}.schema.json).

5827.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
5827.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document’s table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. |   |   | . | Tool | review-sheet-sync | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet-sync.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

5859.content: A review-process task moves one review-comment/1.0.0 todo’s status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through transition(), which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. 5883.content: Write one folio-dublin-core/v1 record and one folio-catalogue-node/v1 item per library entry that the source ledger joins to a CSL-JSON reference, into the folio’s declared catalogue directory, so gen-library-jsonld reads the title from the catalogue’s dc.title instead of falling to the PDF or the slug. 5924.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dublin-core-renderings . Render a catalogue’s Dublin Core records in the two standard forms an outside reader can use: Dublin Core XML, which a harvester reads, and JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. 5971.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
5971.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

5999.title: HCERT library (Rust, native and WebAssembly)
5999.content: The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the hcert world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). Every crate is pinned in Cargo.lock (DEPENDENCIES.md). |   |   | . | Tool | hcert-rust | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-trust-tools/tools/hcert-rust.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/smart-trust-tools/smart-trust-tools.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | smart-trust-tools | . | source | tools/hcert-rust/hcert-rust.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

6133.title: Tools — smart-trust-tools
6133.content: The Tool nodes smart-trust-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 17Tool nodes 16skills satisfied 17invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

6138.title: Tools
6138.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 271Tool nodes 121skills satisfied 240invoked as a shell command 30reachable over MCP

6142.content: The records SMART Trust HCERT library tools (smart-trust-tools) holds in external-schemas, read at this build’s pins. 6144.title: Who declares each specification
6144.content: A user declares the specification it depends on; the record names no user. That is data-modelling step 8 — the dependent holds the pointer — and it is why this list cannot drift from the code: a file that stops declaring stops being listed. Four forms are read: a @conformsTo tag, a conformsTo: front-matter list, an xmlns binding, and a graph typology whose typing module declares the spec (bean u63y). 6148.title: Glossary: Skills
6148.content: Candidate terms extracted from every skill’s front matter: name as the label, description as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. 6188.title: Glossary: Schema fields, T–Z
6188.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 539 terms and is 313 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 539 shown . T U V W

6194.title: Glossary: Schema fields, F–L
6194.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 630 terms and is 371 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 630 shown . F G H I J K L

6203.title: Glossary: Schema fields, D–E
6203.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 214 terms and is 127 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 214 shown . D E

6207.title: Glossary: Schema fields, S
6207.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 270 terms and is 156 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 270 shown . S

6210.title: Glossary: Schema fields, A–C
6210.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 542 terms and is 325 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 542 shown . A B C

6215.title: Glossary: Schema fields, M–O
6215.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 234 terms and is 141 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 234 shown . M N O

6421.title: A
6421.content: ArchiMate model from the glossary candidate, extracted Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without --write it only reports; --check fails when anything would change. --seed goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under library/ (--from): an authored model is never a source of the glossary. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/archimate-from-glossary/archimate-from-glossary.ts#archimate-from-glossary .

6422.content: Bibliography page candidate, extracted Render every reference in the checkout (each declared references directory's folio-reference/v1 nodes and each catalogue directory's Dublin Core records) as the bibliography page and one page per sub-graph, each with its BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core JSON-LD exports and a per-reference export, at the route of the visualiser core declares for it. Block edit and feedback links candidate, extracted Each labelled block's links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor on main, and [feedback] opens a new GitHub issue about the block, from the folio's .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml when it has one (prefilling only the fields it declares: block, section, source, page, url) or as a plain issue whose body carries the same facts. The document build draws these on every block; this Tool prints them as JSON for one block or all. Governed by the block-actions skill. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/block-actions/block-actions.ts#block-actions . BPMN workflow engine candidate, extracted Run a declared BPMN process as an instance: workflow_start opens one for a subject, workflow_next reports what is enabled, workflow_complete records a step or answers a decision (a DMN-computed one from facts) and REFUSES a step that is not enabled. State is committed under the work plan, so which edge was taken is a record, not a memory. Tools of cat-harness-tools · source cat-harness-tools/tools/bpmn-engine/bpmn-engine.ts#bpmn-engine . Build an IG and write its AST candidate, extracted Run one ordinary IG Publisher build through AstPublisher (a subclass that overrides nothing) and write the AST beside output/: one JSON file per resource keyed canonical|version, dependencies.json (upstream's DependencyAnalyser plus the Library/PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition/Measure edges it leaves empty), SUSHI's fsh-index.json, and a manifest that declares itself a cache and records the inputs it is valid for. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/ig-ast-export/ig-ast-export.ts#ig-ast-export . Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration candidate, extracted The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST's resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache's copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES, so the site build reports the IG's own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/ig-repo-site/ig-repo-site.ts#ig-repo-site . Build each IG instance's artefact index from the IG's cached AST candidate, extracted Write each IG instance's fhir-artifact-index/ at publish, so no IG instance commits one. Indexes each instance that needs this layer and whose repository has an AST cache branch; others are skipped and named. Per instance: index.json from the AST ig-cache.sh restore lays down from the IG repository's cache branch (authority: "cache"), menu.json from the IG's sushi-config.yaml at the commit cloned (recording the source.of and source.ref that stage-ig-sites clones from), releases.json from the repository's GitHub releases (a failed read writes nothing, never an empty list), package.tgz from the AST's resources, and the JSON-LD contexts the IG publishes. Build the review sheet's Apps Script and a document's Config tab candidate, extracted Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document's Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio's review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft's pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet's links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document's URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet's Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document's table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. 6423.title: C
6423.content: Catalogue a library from its bibliography candidate, extracted Write one folio-dublin-core/v1 record and one folio-catalogue-node/v1 item per library entry that the source ledger joins to a CSL-JSON reference, into the folio's declared catalogue directory, so gen-library-jsonld reads the title from the catalogue's dc.title instead of falling to the PDF or the slug. The join is exact: a ledger row naming the entry's structure.json source file, one reference id, and the same sha256 where both record one. Unjoined entries are reported and left alone. Never touches a node it did not write. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/catalogue-from-references/catalogue-from-references.ts#catalogue-from-references . Check a Questionnaire field for field against the wireframe it was derived from candidate, extracted Compare the data-element fields of a mid-fidelity wireframe (per data-layout, in document order) with the answerable items of a BUILT Questionnaire (depth first, named by definition or code). Reports a field with no item, an item with no field, an item naming no data element, a data element twice in one layout, and the first place the order differs. Fidelity, not design. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/check-wireframe-questionnaire/check-wireframe-questionnaire.ts#check-wireframe-questionnaire . Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. Cut an IG release as a GitHub draft that carries its packages and AST, and report a version left untagged or unreleased candidate, extracted Gather a release's files from a full Publisher build (package.tgz and its R4/R4B variants, and ast-data.zip, the IG's AST with the Libraries' ELM), say from sushi-config.yaml whether it is a pre-release, and make or refresh the GitHub DRAFT release for the tag with the files uploaded. 6426.title: F
6426.content: FHIR AST cache candidate, extracted Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt AST artefacts for an IG. Always try restore first: a full AST build via AstExportCli is expensive, a restore is fast. seed commits the IG API a layer above generates from the AST (ig-site:sidecars, via ig-api-cache.ts) as ig-api/ beside it, and the artefact index built from that tree (ig-index-cache.ts) as fhir-artifact-index/index.json, so a site reads both by raw URL at the cache commit. Figure coverage and computability candidate, extracted For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Exits non-zero when any declared figure is missing; --require-computable also fails on pictures, linked or not. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/figure-coverage/figure-coverage.ts#figure-coverage . Freshness is the QA sweep's own rule, including the uses-graph hash for graph-scoped criteria. Runs no checker and writes no verdict. 6432.title: R
6432.content: Rank candidate glossary terms in prose by C-value candidate, extracted The scoring step of the automatic-term-extraction method: count the word n-grams of one or more Markdown or text files (not across punctuation, front matter or code), and rank them by C-value as Frantzi & Ananiadou 1996 define it, so nested multi-word terms are not swamped by the longer phrases that contain them. Tested against the paper's own worked example (Table 2). Every row is a candidate; it writes nothing and promotes nothing. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/c-value-terms/c-value-terms.ts#c-value-terms . Rebuild only the cone of a change and merge it into the AST candidate, extracted Write the unchanged part of a base AST as a FHIR package into the package cache, build a temporary IG of only the rebuild set with the stock Publisher, merge the result into a mixed-provenance AST (builtAt per resource), and repeat while the merged graph's cone reaches resources that were not rebuilt. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/ig-ast-incremental-build/ig-ast-incremental-build.ts#ig-ast-incremental-build . 6437.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, R–Z
6437.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 367 terms and is 310 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 367 shown . R S T U V W

6438.content: Raise a finding against the wrong side candidate, extracted The prose and the code really disagree: raise a finding that names which side is wrong and why. Usually the prose, because the code is what runs — but a skill can state intended behaviour correctly while the code has regressed, and then the finding is against the code. Raised, never silently fixed — a reviewer who re-themes a note has substituted their judgement for the author's without saying so. The sweep runs daily and proposes; this acts. Between them a branch can come back to life — bean w2g5 documents exactly that, a session reusing one branch across five successive pull requests. Says agree, disagree or unknown; unknown (could not run) is said as plainly as a disagreement, because the table reads both the same way and an unknown read as agreement certifies on one party's word. Re-materialize and record new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . Each re-pin PR is itself a merge to main and runs this process again. When the re-pin moves a layer whose software-library nodes are derived at the pin (bootstrap-tools, whose nodes cat-harness-tools holds in libraries/held/), the same PR runs bun run cat libraries:derive, and libraries:check fails until it does (owner, 2026-10-30, bootstrap-tools#44). None found is recorded with where it looked. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Repin . The host consumes it as a remote mount (a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json) if it imports its code, or a subscription if it only reads its content, pinned to a commit while staging. Read each queued PR's live facts candidate, extracted From GitHub and the checkout, now: authored paths, shared declarations, size, conflict risk and overlap KIND against the other queued PRs (T3), own CI and whether it ran on the head (T2). Tools: merge:overlap for the overlap facts, check:head-has-run for ownCi. Nothing read here is written to a queue entry; it is the input to the placement table. ownCi IS NOT A VERDICT READ. Never ask whether anything is red: ask which workflow runs are OWED for the head's event and whether each one is present and successful. The two readings come apart, measured 2026-10-02 on #1889's head 7ab6119405 -- 9 runs present, all 9 gating job NAMES matching, 3 of them in_progress with a null conclusion, and 3 check SUITES completed as action_required having executed nothing.
