Review increment (test behaviour) candidate, extracted Inner loop: the BA tests each delivered increment against the acceptance criteria. They do not review code — they test behaviour. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#BA_ReviewIncrement . Review requirements and impact analysis candidate, extracted The BA reviews the formal requirements and the impact analysis the agent produced. When a requirement changes a rendered surface, the BA (or the requester) also reviews the wireframe candidates, web and mobile, shown wherever the requester will look (the conversation, the issue, the pull request, or several) with staging deep links and screenshots, and chooses one before implementation starts. The agent records the choice; it never makes it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#BA_ReviewReqs . Review staged rendering candidate, extracted Author reviews the rendered feature branch at <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/ and compares against the main site. The staging banner shows the commit SHA. The agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) sits beside the URLs, with its counts and status line. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewStaging . Review synthesised needs statement candidate, extracted The BA reviews what the agent synthesised and checks it against what they actually need. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#BA_ReviewNeeds . Review the adoption candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#O_Review . Review the change candidate, extracted A human or an agent acting AS reviewer. Nothing is a reviewer; somebody acts as one for the duration of this lane. For a rendered change the reviewer reads the agent's before/after preview rather than building one. On agent-touched changes, an adversarial code review evaluates against the RED FLAG taxonomy and writes a committed verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Review . Review the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-committee.bpmn: compare staged against main, slice the change and review each slice, settle withdrawals and disputes, gate on coverage, review the impact, and either approve or request changes. The one judgement inside it is Call_Adjudication, whose stands / withdrawn this call accepts; public-comment, which calls this whole process, reaches it through here. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_CommitteeReview . Review the change set on its staging preview candidate, extracted The content-change review of the author's branch: its PR lists the PC refs it answers, and its staging preview is the after side of every deep link. A change the reviewers send back returns to the author inside that process. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#CallActivity_ChangeSet . Review the draft publication candidate, extracted Content reviewer, QC reviewer and technical officer review the draft as a whole — coherence, phase-gate criteria, breaking vs non-breaking change. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_ReviewDraft . Review the editorial dependencies candidate, extracted uses[] is what a READER must have read to follow the block — never populated from the formal dependency graph. Once every changed block is covered, the committee checks the editorial dependencies of the change as a whole before judging its impact. Reading order is a property of folio content, so the step belongs to the content process, which reaches the harness's review by calling DOWN into review-task. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Task_ReviewUses . Review the existing guidance candidate, extracted The author reads what the document, DAK or IG ALREADY says on this question, before looking outward. A recommendation that contradicts a sibling recommendation in the same artefact is a defect no external evidence will reveal. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_ReviewExisting . Review the filed requirement, sign off candidate, extracted The Business Analyst / Owner reviews the filed requirement in docs/requirements/<slug>.md, its concern-group organisation in docs/requirements/index.md, its three-axis traceability, and any supersession or retirement update, deciding approve, amend, reject, defer, or cancel. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#BA_ReviewFiling . Review the findings candidate, extracted THE GATE: the editor sees every finding BEFORE anything reaches the corpus. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviewFindings . Review the impact with stakeholders candidate, extracted The committee reads the old version, the new version and each affected adaptation side by side on the staging preview, and hears the adaptation team's account of what rests on them. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Review . Review the MVP against what we bind to candidate, extracted A narrower question than "is the new version good": does everything in binds still hold, checked against the deployed page. A userTask, and the lane admits person and agent — a review agent is a legitimate reviewer here, and the separation that matters is the next lane's: a reviewer cannot accept. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#R_Review . Review the PR; merge or close candidate, extracted The maintainer checks that the PR writes down what the issue decided and nothing else, lets the layer's checks run, and merges or closes it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_Merge . Review the preview and answer candidate, extracted Members read the preview and answer in their Blue columns, or leave them as they are when the change is right. They record the row's Disposition (Blue): Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_AnswerPreview . Review the schema definition node candidate, extracted Does the node declare what KIND of node it is? Does a widened type carry its mirrors? Does a removed field leave a reason behind, so the next author does not re-add it in good faith? And where the node RENDERS to something the site serves — a colour, a glyph, a theme's tokens — does a Tool maintain that artefact, and does the visual fact have only one home? The node decides; the stylesheet reports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewSchema . Review the site's size candidate, extracted Read the size report the build printed before its push, and fix what it shows, or raise a decision card with the owner when no known fix applies (skill ig-publication §"Size review"). The report is cat-harness-tools site-size.ts (bun run cat site:size), written as site-size.json beside the build, never into the site. It gives the total against the published gh-pages root, the top directories, the size by extension, the biggest files, byte-identical duplicates, source maps, the directories named after another layer of index.lock.json, and the directories the shared-assets host could serve. Growth over the budget (10% or 10 MB) is a warning. The review is advisory and never refuses a publish. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_SizeReview . Review the size against its budget candidate, extracted The index flags an app over its sizeBudgetMB; the site size review reads it with the rest of the site. Over budget is a finding for the author, never a silent publish. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Size . Review the staged form and wireframe candidate, extracted At the deep links. A change is requested through ✍ suggest in its Questionnaire mode, or the questionnaire-change issue form, and says which side was edited: the Questionnaire or the wireframe. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewStaged . Review the Tool node candidate, extracted Does it name skills, and do they resolve? Is the mechanism it advertises the one that actually runs? Are its IRIs minted rather than written out? And the question a covered skill hides: is the COMMAND reachable, or only the skill satisfied? A skill can be served by the neighbours of its mechanism while the mechanism itself is reachable from no node, and check:tools reports it as covered and is right to. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewTool . Review the translation candidate, extracted Coverage, preserved terms and echoes are mechanical. A semantic round trip needs a back-translator that has not seen the original; where none has run, the criterion carries no verdict and that is the honest state. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_ReviewTranslation . Review translation for accuracy candidate, extracted A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translated markdown for: - Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology - Preservation of meaning from the source - Cultural appropriateness for the target locale - Consistency with the domain glossary For WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements ("SHALL", "SHOULD", "MAY") are translated with the correct force in the target language. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_SMEReview . Review what the substrate offers candidate, extracted Every subgraph, asset class and harness the cached declaration names, each with its current state — referenced, materialised, unknown, stale, or refused by a gate. Shown whole, because a reader who sees only what was chosen cannot tell "not offered" from "not taken". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Review . Revise the adaptations as decided candidate, extracted Each revision is an ordinary content change, reviewed on its staging preview through content change review, on the re-pin's branch or a branch that merges with it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Revise . Revise the proposed change candidate, extracted The editor chose revise: rework the proposed change against the findings the editor reviewed, then send it back through validation as a new proposal. The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviseEdit . Root-cause the failure candidate, extracted "Flake" is not a root cause. A red PR is work now, whatever its review state — only a green, mergeable head waits on reviewers. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Diagnose . Round trip on the changed strings candidate, extracted The untainted round trip, with the sample restricted to the strings this run translated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Call_TR_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate the target-language .md into the source language and compare the meaning with the original. It catches semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see, and tells the two apart. Tool: the translation_validate MCP tool. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_RoundTripQa . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, "route drift to a human reviewer"), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. The findings include translation:glossary:check's: every glossary term translated against the locale term base, fixed before sign-off, with its glossary section in the KG QA report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block's <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO's msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means "not yet run", which is never a pass. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA (back-translate) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Route every climb through platform.ts candidate, extracted Every platform symbol the sub-KG uses is re-exported from <name>/platform.ts, so re-pointing the platform is a one-file edit. A merge from main is where new climbs arrive; reroute them here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seam . Route it, and watch the queue candidate, extracted A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. Acquisition stops here — the moment a file is in the queue, library-ingestion owns it, and keeping that seam sharp is what lets a resource acquired through a channel that does not exist yet reach ingestion unchanged. An arrival may be minutes or days away, so it is watched rather than chased. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Route . Route the answer back, quoted candidate, extracted On answerRoute, with the person's own message attached by id where the host allows, so the sibling can treat it as the person's approval. A paraphrase is never approval. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_RouteBack . Run check:ci-health, WRITING the report file candidate, extracted Run check:ci-health --out, writing the report file before any exit path. Exit 0 clean, 1 live failures, 2 could not check. bun also exits 1 on an uncaught exception, so an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-check. Where its verdict comes from: Asked of the verdict output that the check step of .github/workflows/ci-health.yml writes, not of the raw exit code. check:ci-health exits 0 clean, 1 live failure(s), 2 could not check; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is reclassified as could-not-check, as is any other code. no is verdict == 'unknown': the last step runs exit 1 and no issue step runs, so the tracking issue is left untouched. yes is verdict != 'unknown', the guard on the label step and so on both issue paths. Weekly, also measure each workflow's job shape (owner, 2026-11-13, card "A. Collapse into one job"): from the Actions API, each job's queue wait (started_at minus created_at) and run time (completed_at minus started_at), as medians over recent default-branch runs. A job whose median wait exceeds its run time, or a serial chain of more than 2 jobs each under 1 minute, is a candidate to fold into one job as steps: open a work item naming it. Heavy or parallel shards, jobs with other permissions or runners, and jobs whose check names merge:guard, branch protection or verdict reuse read stay separate (skill ci-health). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run every verifier over the export candidate, extracted Run the verifier set (scripts/publish-verify.ts, bun run cat publish:verify -- --dir <site>) over the built tree. A SET: each verifier is one entry, and adding one changes nothing else. The first is JSON-LD expansion under a real processor, network refused — a property the context does not declare, a relative IRI or a context that will not load is a finding. Only documents of OURS are verified; third-party data in the tree is counted and cannot block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/publish-verification.bpmn#A_Verify . Run IG release (draft) by hand for the tag candidate, extracted Actions → "IG release (draft)" → Run workflow, input tag = v<version>. For a tag pushed before the IG carried the caller, or whose run failed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-release.bpmn#Task_RunRelease . Run main's checks candidate, extracted The merge starts main's checks. Until tools#1384, a closed PR's run can cancel them, so the steward re-runs a cancelled main run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn#Task_MainRun . Run placement, file a bean candidate, extracted The offer produces a DECISION, not a node. placement then decides layer, graph and node kind — it is the step that catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio — and the authoring itself becomes a bean, because work here is a bean before it is a file. op="note" and not create, for the reason A_CreateBeans above states: the engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean. The agent mints the authoring bean itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first, and what this step records is a note that the decision was taken. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_RecordKg . Run publication QA gates candidate, extracted Publication-readiness QA across layers — QC reports, IG Publisher QA, proof status, broken links, build warnings. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_PublicationQa . Run QC gates on the aggregate QA candidate, extracted qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone's rows first. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Qa . Run the deterministic gates candidate, extracted Template currency, catalogue coverage, placeholder, tag and URL preservation, officiality, kg:locale, and the locale's supplements compiling with no SUSHI error and passing their structural checks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Gates . Run the gate set on the train candidate, extracted Every gate CI runs, on the combination (R2): a member that passes alone can still break main with another. The merge-gate epic (nok9, #1887) adds its gates here when they land. The release security gate (bun run cat security:gate, bean ieum) is one of them: it runs inside the gate set, so no train merges past a blocking security finding or a security check that could not run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_Gates . Run the gates against the merge of head into base candidate, extracted CI tests the MERGE, not the branch. That is why a locally green tree can go red here: the agent's tree and the merge result are different trees, and the difference is invisible from a checkout. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunCI . Run the health checks, keeping the report either way candidate, extracted Run bun run cat health --out and upload the JSON report whatever the verdict — on unknown it is the only evidence of why the sweep went blind. Exit 0 clean, 1 gating findings, 2 could not check; exit 1 with no report is a crash. The checks report and never act: every finding names something a person does. Where its verdict comes from: Asked of the verdict output of 'Run the health checks' in .github/workflows/health-check.yml, which runs bun run cat health --out. Exit 0 is clean, 1 gating finding(s), 2 could not check; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is reclassified as could-not-check, as is any other code. no is verdict == 'unknown': 'Refuse to report success on an unchecked repository' runs exit 1 and the tracking issue is left untouched. yes is verdict != 'unknown', the guard on ensuring the repo-health label. The report is uploaded as an artifact on every verdict (if: always()), including this one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run the node audits candidate, extracted check:tools, kg:audit and typecheck. Read the kg-qa sidecar rather than the summary: it is written per node so an inherited defect and a new one are distinguishable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RunNodeAudits . Run the platform's own gates candidate, extracted Before pushing, not after CI says so. bun test passing is NOT the gates passing: measured 2026-09-19, a green unit suite sat beside a tsc failure and a missing @graphNode tag, and the second broke a QA sidecar comparison as well — one cause, two symptoms, and an agent running only the tests would have pushed all three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunGates . Run the release security gate candidate, extracted bun run cat security:gate, before the site is built. It runs every security check the repository names: workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile and toolchain pins, QA reviewer permission, materialised fixity, and third-party action SHA pinning outside staging-only workflows. Each reports pass, fail or unknown; a blocking fail or unknown refuses the publish. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_SecurityGate . Run the requirements check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat check:requirements to verify schema conformance (bootstrap/schemas/requirement.schema.json), slug uniqueness across docs/proposals/ and docs/requirements/, acyclicity of derivedFrom, existence of all referenced derivedFrom / dependsOn / supersededBy / skills / processes targets, and RequirementSet sign-off invariants. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_RunCheck . Run the review-log-watch check candidate, extracted Runs Tool review-log-watch with the folio repository, the saved values and the log's state file. The tool reads the repository's open and closed issues (no pull requests, no issue labelled no-sheet) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human), Change Set (human)) with the last check's. A read with no Issue column tracks only change-set issues and appends no rows, reporting them as issue-unlinked. It writes nothing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_RunCheck . Run the row's gates tests · e2e · site-links candidate, extracted The mvp commands declared for this tenant. For the theme: bun test, CI=1 bunx playwright test (a11y, action tiles, sidebar panels, QA panel) and scripts/site-links.ts --site ./_site, which checks the navbar tiles against the BUILT site rather than against the attribute — the distinction that let a 404 ship unnoticed once already. A red gate is EVIDENCE, not an exit. It does not end the process and it does not loop by itself: "this version breaks us" is a finding the decider needs, not a reason to stop before they see it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Gates . Run the rule's mechanical half candidate, extracted Whatever patterns and terminology the rule carries. A judgementOnly rule has no mechanical half by declaration, which is different from nobody having written one yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_MechanicalHalf .

6439.title: S
6439.content: Saturation meta-merge candidate, extracted Offer the card and land only on the owner's tap. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Call_Meta . Say it could not be confirmed candidate, extracted No URL, no probe, or a failed request. Reported as "could not check", never as "not yet" and never as "live". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportUnknown . Say what is being decided, and why it matters now candidate, extracted First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_GiveContext . Say what moved and where it went candidate, extracted Tell the reader what moved and where it went, so the content can be found in the trashcan rather than inferred missing from a card that disappeared. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_ReportMove . Say where it will be candidate, extracted A measured 404. The author is told the address and that the first build has not landed there yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportPending . Scaffold the folio candidate, extracted folio_init writes content/, uploads/, library/, the manifests, the builder shim and AGENTS.md. Skipped when the folio already exists. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scaffold the folio (folio_init) candidate, extracted content/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, <slug>.json and index.config.json (the layer's config inline in its entry; no <slug>.config.json), the builder shim, AGENTS.md with its stubs, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store. On the overlay path it declares in index.config.json exactly the markers picked at Task_ChooseHarnessed, and none it was not given. Refuses rather than overwrites when a folio is already present. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scan open issues for match candidate, extracted Search open issues, then recently closed ones, by title and body keywords for one this request belongs to. Requirements may span several issues; note every relevant one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_ScanIssues . Scan the environment opportunities and threats candidate, extracted The external axis, first, per Weihrich. Work the source's categories of environmental change rather than free-associating: societal, governmental, economic, competitive, supplier and market changes, each item recorded with what it impacts. An opportunity is an external element that gives benefit; a threat is one that could cause trouble. Both are outside the subject and largely beyond its control — that is what puts them on this axis, not whether they feel good or bad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanExternal . Scan the repo for content worth importing candidate, extracted Read-only. Classifies candidates into library/ (external source) and content/ (authored here), and reports what it could not classify as its own bucket rather than forcing every file into one of the two. Its fourth section, markers, lists the content markers it found — sushi-config.yaml, a legacy dak.json, .bpmn processes, a beans store, library/, Lean, folio manifests — each with its paths, whether index.config.json already declares it (declared, not-declared, or unknown), and the snippet that would. bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/scan-repo-content.ts --json, a plain command any agent host can run. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ScanRepo . Scan the subject strengths and weaknesses candidate, extracted The internal axis. Work the source's functional checklist rather than a blank page: marketing, research and development, management information systems, management team, operations, finance, human resources. A strength gives advantage over others in the field; a weakness places the subject at a disadvantage relative to others. Both are attributes OF the subject. The source's warning belongs to this step specifically: listing strengths on paper "is very different from testing the organization and experiencing the strengths at work", so a strength recorded here is a claim, and where evidence for it exists it is cited. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanInternal . Schedule the refresh watcher candidate, extracted Schedule a fresh session that follows translation-refresh on each layer, so a template that moves after today is caught by its check failing, not by a reader. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's. Write the design intent candidate, extracted A short statement of who the screen is for, what they need to do, and what it must show. It is the criterion every candidate is judged against. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Intent . Write the entry and cache the declaration candidate, extracted The subscriptions entry in the subscriber's layer declaration — id, repository, ref, and nothing chosen yet — plus a cached copy of the substrate's declaration at the pin. The entry holds the choice and the pin, never state: whether a part is held is answered by its materialisation record, and a second answer here would be free to disagree with it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Record . Write the entry that LEADS — keeping the checker's beneath it candidate, extracted Not relaxable, and the one step here that is not. A judgement nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from a checker that was never run, so the judgement is free and the record is not. Do not resolve the disagreement away: both entries stay, the adjudication on top under the sweep's most-recent-matching-hash rule. A disagreement between a checker and a reviewer is information, and somebody re-running the check next month needs to find that a checker read it differently rather than a clean pass. /api/relevance/adjudicate reached the same rule independently — human_adjudicated written alongside, never over, the agent's assessed_by. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_RecordEntry . Write the first candidate as a fuzzy msgstr candidate, extracted Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation. The first candidate becomes the msgstr, marked #, fuzzy: the page shows it, the status page counts it as needing review, and it stays the default until a person adjudicates the catalogue. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_SeedFuzzy . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_QAReport . Write the lock candidate, extracted index.lock.json beside the downstream's index.config.json (the legacy <instance>.mount-lock.json is still read, and is renamed onto the new name when rewritten; both present is an error): the pins it was written for, each layer's repository, SHA and how the pin was found, each directory's tree digest — and what was NOT mounted, with why, so an offline check cannot read a gap as clean. Whoever writes the lock writes its layers cache ref (layers:publish, which refuses unless every mount hashes to the lock); on main, the index's workflow does it. Write the note into the folio — with no coordinate candidate, extracted A new note: write it into the folio with no x, no y, no board and no position. A folio is complete with no board, and one note may sit on several boards, which a coordinate on the note could not express. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-place-note.bpmn#A_CreateNote . Either way an entry is appended to the catalogue's translation-qa attestation (criterion human-adjudication) naming the issue and the hash the person saw; the attestation is append-only and checked against qa-attestations/v1 before it is written. The PO header X-Folio-Official and the locale's status.json are never touched. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_Write . It carries a LINK to the harness that was installed and the OVERALL install status across every location — WHEN ABSENT, never replacing: where a README is already there, the link and status go in a marker pair the harness's own README tool maintains. Choose the heavy fields by kg-export §"What is heavy": a heavy field is a payload_sha256 pointer, never a stored column. Never copy the builder. No verdict in it may name the system under test as its reviewer. Writes a folio-test-run/v1 and a test-report/v1. All by REFERENCE: the bean and the instance are each the authority on themselves, and a status copied here would be free to contradict them. NO cat-harness.processes:bean on this step. 6445.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
6445.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 294 terms and is 246 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 294 shown . 0–9 A B C D

6446.content: 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Extract .

6447.title: A
6447.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Abort . Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Address the review candidate, extracted Every finding is answered — implemented, or replied to with why not. A design question does not excuse skipping the nits in the same review. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_AddressReview . Adjudicate against the checker candidate, extracted The reviewer and a checker read the same claim differently — a disagreement about ONE kg-qa criterion (prose-claims-resolve). Descend into Process_CriterionAdjudication, which runs the shared adjudication and then one of its three outcomes: the checker's finding stands, the criterion is scoped, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The checker's entry is kept beneath the verdict rather than overwritten (requirement R4 of issue #1042). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the voice findings candidate, extracted Three outcomes, all legitimate: the register is wrong for this genre; the criterion does not belong in this genre and should carry profiles; or the block is a stated exception and a reviewer entry records why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_AdjudicateVoice . Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Admit it to the train, record the train id candidate, extracted Writes the queue entry's trainId and placement (rule, class, rank) with who decided and when. A decision, so it is stored; the facts it was decided on are not. PRECONDITION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the worktree carries no untracked, non-ignored file before the member is merged and the tree regenerated. git status --porcelain must be empty. The reason is specific: generated directory READMEs carry a per-subdirectory file count, and the writer counts the files GIT WOULD COMMIT -- git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard (bootstrap-tools/scripts/git-files.ts:23). --exclude-standard already keeps IGNORED junk out, which is the __pycache__ case that drove that line, but --others still counts an untracked file nobody has ignored. So a transient written by an earlier train step moves a committed count, readme:subgraphs:check goes red, and the red belongs to nobody. Train 6 hit this. The count is volatile for a second reason the precondition cannot fix: two members each adding a file write different integers to one line. Measured in bean y7b3 -- 76 of 300 replayed merges conflicted on beans/README.md, every one on the | defs/ | N files | line -- and the exposure is wider than that bean states: 54 generated READMEs across 14 layers carry 207 such rows (measured 2026-10-02). merge:main already resolves them (readme-generated-regions), so the cost falls on merges made by plain git. The chosen fix is bean ba9e: take the integer off main into the KG's _data layer, which classifies take-base and is therefore auto-resolved, leaving the README with a marker that is invariant until the directory crosses LIST_LIMIT. Not done here -- it spans the pinned bootstrap-tools submodule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Admit . Adopt the version bump candidate, extracted The reusable subprocess. Every pinned dependency enters it the same way, so a new tenant is a registry row and a call — never a second diagram saying the same thing in different words. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Call_Adopt . Adopt, hold or decline candidate, extracted A PERSON decides. The lane admits person only, so activity-fulfilment-kind fails the moment somebody makes an agent the accepting party, and relaxable="false" means no package may relax the step. The publication manager rather than the editor because a pin is not a change to the corpus — it is a change to what the published artefact is BUILT FROM, and that role is the one accountable for what is live. Deliberately NOT a DMN-backed gateway. Every computed gateway in this repository reduces to arithmetic over tool output; this one weighs a rendering nobody can score against the cost of staying behind, and a table here would look authoritative without being so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#PM_Decide . Agent pass on the changed rows candidate, extracted For each changed row, the agent pass of Contributor feedback on a working draft: Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, Ready for merge = Yes its merge, and a Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook), every row with an empty Feedback (agent) and every row whose Blue cells changed gets feedback in the same wake, in the fixed layout: the ask first (Decision needed: with lettered options, one recommended, and where to answer), then Proposed direction: and Next:, only the tags bold. The work stays inside the row's Selected Sections; a row with none gets a question asking which, and any edit outside them is named on an Outside the selected sections: line. PRs are named as repo#n, which the sheet script links, and it adds a Where to review line linking each selected section on the preview. The agent then runs tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts and fixes what it flags: a cell that breaks the layout, or a PR state that GitHub contradicts. The agent records its step on the Agent tab at once, with the real time. Previews follow main: by default (Config PREVIEW_REFRESH automatic) the agent runs tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts on every poll for every open change-set PR, and also when people act on a change set (new Blue feedback, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback asking to update the preview); with PREVIEW_REFRESH on-feedback, only then. A branch behind main gets main merged in (a merge commit), pushed and restaged; a conflict a person must settle is asked in the change set's feedback. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_AgentPass . Agent review of the change candidate, extracted A review agent judges what no checker can: accuracy, voice, exposition, whether the change says what the editor meant. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_AgentReview . Agree each change-set's requirements on its issue candidate, extracted A change-set gets its primary GitHub issue the first time somebody engages with it (the Discuss form, a recommendation or decision on one of its comments, a mention, a PR), opened by the folio's public-comment workflow; any number of other issues may discuss it and are linked. People agree the requirements there, and the committee or editor changes the record with cs-add / cs-remove / cs-title / cs-requirements / cs-committee / cs-merge / cs-split / cs-close / cs-new. Making change-sets is people's, in any of three ways, each like opening an issue: a row on the review sheet's Review Change Sets with only a Title (the sheet script gives it the next id), a change-set issue from the folio's change-set issue form, or feedback that says a change-set should be split, merged or moved. For the last two the agent proposes the change-sets and which comments go where, as a Decision needed question, and makes them only once an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. A comment is moved by typing another change-set's id, or new, in Change Set (human). The issue's change-set section is rendered from the record and put back if hand-edited; the nightly reconcile keeps every issue in line. The issue is for requirements; the PR that closes it is for preview, review and approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_GroupChangeSets . Agree the release date and comment period candidate, extracted The review committee and the editor agree when the public comment release goes out and when comment closes. Skill: public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_AgreeReleaseDate . Alert the publication manager candidate, extracted Process_PublishAlert — the ONE alert every failing step after the publish button goes through, whichever step it was. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Call_Alert . Announce and note the merge manager candidate, extracted Send "merge manager: <session id>" to every sibling and the owner, and note it durably on the coordination work item, so it is used by all, including siblings started later. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Announce . Announce the branch on the issue candidate, extracted On CREATING the feature branch, comment on the issue: the branch name, the process and phase, and the beans claimed. Visibility is the whole point — without it a sibling session or a human cannot tell that work has begun, only that it has finished. Deliberately on this edge and not inside Phase 6. The three loops back into A_Implement (increment rejected, MVP not ready, feedback translated) re-enter implementation on the SAME branch, and re-announcing on each would be noise. Announce once, when the branch is created. Before announcing, run the collision review that starts any new unit of work (coordinate, "Starting new work"): open PRs and in-progress beans checked against the branch's files and subject, scaled to the blast radius, and the result recorded in the bean before the first edit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_AnnounceBranch . Announce the hand-over candidate, extracted Tell every sibling and the owner, and update the durable note with the session that holds the lane now. Nobody merges between holders. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Task_Lapse . Answer the other four gates candidate, extracted Restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, each answered permitted, refused or unknown. They are four answers to one decision, and Gateway_Gates reads them with size through decisions/materialization-gate.dmn. RESTRICTIONS. 'No restrictions known in context' is a STATE, not a green light. GateVerdict is three-valued for this reason alone, and unknown is never rendered as permitted. COPYRIGHT. What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. RETENTION. A copy with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one — the same argument bean-blocking makes about a block with no expiry. An ARCHIVAL copy is the exception and it is a specification rather than an omission: freshness() reports it permanent, not no-expiry. SOURCE LOSS. Not hypothetical. The one IRIS record this repository holds carries a handle on iris.wpro.who.int, a regional instance merged into the global one. Only an ARCHIVAL copy of the original bytes discharges this; a working copy cannot, because the derived sections are not the publication. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_AnswerGates . Answer, decline, or say nothing candidate, extracted The Requestor's move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation's "if there is no answer" was for. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_Answer . Append removed with the reason candidate, extracted BEFORE the removal, not after: a job that dies mid-step must leave a record of the intent rather than an artefact that vanished with no entry. A reason is REQUIRED — an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity this log exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRemoved . Append rendered candidate, extracted A re-deploy is a rendering, so it gets its own entry rather than overwriting the last. "When was this last built" is then answerable without diffing commits. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRendered . Append rendered to the render log candidate, extracted Its OWN commit, not part of the deploy. The publish action writes only into destination_dir, so an entry riding in _site would land at branches/<slug>/_render-log/ — inside the directory a cleanup removes, which is the one place a record of the removal must not be. continue-on-error: a preview that deployed and whose entry did not is a gap in the record, not a failed deploy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_LogRendered . Append restored candidate, extracted A full-replace deploy (docs-site.yml, the only publisher without keep_files) wipes the branch; restore-staging carries the previews AND this log back in. Its own event rather than a second rendered, because "somebody pushed this branch" and "an unrelated merge nearly deleted it" are different facts.
