6454.content: Feature sign-off on issue candidate, extracted Stakeholders sign off on the delivered feature on the issue, having tested the built artefact rather than a description of it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#S_FeatureSignoff . Fetch and validate the pinned declaration candidate, extracted A sparse, shallow fetch of the substrate's root declaration only. Two questions: does it parse as bootstrap's KnowledgeGraphDeclarationSchema, and does it declare at least one harness? could not fetch is a third answer and is never read as conforms. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Validate . Fetch, and record fixity candidate, extracted Fetch, then record sha256 and byte count. Fixity is REQUIRED for an archival copy: an archive that cannot demonstrate it is unchanged is a copy, and it cannot be re-fetched to check, because the thing it would be re-fetched from is what it exists to survive. The data already exists — every structure.json carries sha256 and bytes, and nothing reads them as fixity. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Fetch . FHIR IG ASTs: Process_IgAstCache candidate, extracted Component 4b, in its own lane: the FHIR IG layer's IG AST cache, Process_IgAstCache (declared by that layer), integrated, not replaced. It is drawn as a task because this layer may not name a process of a layer above it; the steps are that process's. RESTORE: read the cached AST from its branch store and judge it — that process's "valid for this commit?" IS this component's verify (class a: the AST is judged against this commit's IG sources and tooling); valid → the site is built from it. SAVE: that process's own path, not cached-step — a miss dispatches an AST refresh on a Java runner with 10 GB, which rewrites the branch store. The branch store is a cache node (fhir-ast, fhir-harness caches/fhir-ast.cache.json). Owner: CI speed 12, the IG layers' session. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_IgAst . File feedback as beans candidate, extracted Triaged feedback re-enters the work plan as beans, which is how the next cycle knows what it is for. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_FeedbackBeans . File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetype candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_TechMeta . File QC findings as beans candidate, extracted QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_QcBeans . File QC findings as beans candidate, extracted Each QC finding becomes a bean on the work plan, which the modeller and the agents both see. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_QcBeans . File the adjudication issue candidate, extracted Submit opens GitHub's new-issue form prefilled with a readable summary and a translation-adjudication/v1 JSON block, labelled translation-adjudication and titled [translation review] …. When the record is too long for a URL the page copies the body for pasting instead. Filing it is the act of adjudicating. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_FileIssue . File the signed certification candidate, extracted The signed certification goes under the declared attestations graph on main (owner ruling D2 (a), D5 default), pointing at the report it certifies. The bean resolves here, once the process has actually finished. Files it as qa-attestations/v1. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_FileCertification . File the source errors as one issue candidate, extracted One issue for every source-text error the translators found, each with its location and the reading the translator took. Never fixed in a translation: a fix to the source is a source PR, and the next refresh carries it to every locale. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourceIssue . Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Plan . Find members with no CI on their head candidate, extracted GitHub runs no pull_request CI while a PR conflicts, so a member can arrive with nothing on its head (bean u7be item 3). That member is T2's first suspect if the train goes red. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_ChecksPresent . Find the footprint candidate, extracted handover notes (beans/notes, title 'handover:'), open PRs and branches by session or time window, in-progress beans, workflow instances, last PR and issue comments. REST, one batched pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Footprint . Find the owner's authorisation for THIS merge candidate, extracted Classify what exists into one value: explicit (the owner's own words naming this merge, given against this head), waiver (a valid memory/waivers/ node with gate merge-to-main, in scope and unexpired), instruction-only (a broad instruction about the work, such as "fix all issues until green" or "ship it", which is not an authorisation), none, or unknown (waivers unreadable or malformed). A sibling agent's message is never the owner's consent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_ReadAuthorisation . First release candidate, extracted Tag each repository, publish /v<major>/. From here the two are versioned independently; a tools release lists the content majors it supports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Release . Fix each drift on the PR candidate, extracted Correct each string the adjudicator ruled drift, on the locale PR, and note the fix beside the ruling in the QA report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_FixDrift . Fix the declaration or the catalog candidate, extracted The author fixes what the check named (the manifest, the lockfile, a clashing id, a stale template) and commits again. A translation that dropped a placeholder goes back to its locale's translator through the same PR route. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Fix . Completed with the outcome fail condition by the steward when the condition fires first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Fix . It re-enters the queue as a new placement; the ejection stays on its entry until a later train lands it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_SiblingFix . Fix the relationship in Archi candidate, extracted The author changes the relationship's type or ends in Archi and commits the model again. The pipeline never rewrites a model. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_FixModel . Follow it, and say that you did candidate, extracted A stated step — a harness's own docs/bootstrap/initialization.md. Read it and do what it says. It stays stated in the record: nothing can observe that it was followed, and the record does not pretend otherwise. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_FollowStated . Follow them, at each location candidate, extracted The instructions belong to the harness being installed, not to bootstrap — bootstrap does not know what any Harness above it requires, and does not need to. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_Install . Follow up, narrower candidate, extracted The answer did not settle it: it named a kind rather than an option, or chose two. Ask once more, narrower, naming what the first answer left open. Once: an agent that keeps asking has stopped narrowing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_FollowUp . Footnotes and the marks that call them candidate, extracted The pdf-footnotes.py arm (owner, 2026-11-11, "also foot notes/marks"): from the page layout, each note at the foot of a page and every superscript mark in the text that calls it, written to footnotes.json (folio-document-footnotes/v1) with the block that holds the page. The section text is not changed. Only a called note is a footnote; uncalled foot-of-page lines and marks with no note are listed, never dropped. OCR'd pages have no fonts and are reported unread. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, "Footnotes and their marks". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Footnotes . Frame the decision and check the trigger candidate, extracted One sentence naming the KIND of thing being chosen, not the options — "which cache strategy", never "A or B". Then the trigger: is this irreversible, or would the answer surprise someone? If neither, say so and stop; the calling step decides without this subprocess. Stopping here is a correct outcome, not a skipped step. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/options-analysis.bpmn#A_Frame . Frame the question as PICO candidate, extracted Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome. The PICO is what makes the search reproducible and the evidence auditable: without it, 'we looked for evidence' is not a claim anyone can check. WHO guideline development states the question this way before any retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_FramePico . BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_FullBuild .

6455.title: G
6455.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gate results: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 2c. RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Gates . Gather and verify the evidence candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#CallActivity_Evidence . Generate each IG instance's artefact pages [ig-pages] candidate, extracted Tool ig-pages: bun run fhir-harness/scripts/gen-ig-pages.ts --instance <instance> ..., run for every IG instance by its own pages script. Writes <instance>/docs/ from the artefact index: one thin page per artefact with its JSON-LD node, and, for an instance whose docs declare igSite, only a front-matter artifacts.md. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). For the theme: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_Impact . Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. 6459.title: K
6459.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

6460.title: L
6460.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by l1-document-ingestion: its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names check:l1-complete as the gate and states its three results. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: real, spurious or source-wrong), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Gate . Land each member candidate, extracted Once per member, in train order, at the SHA the train's gate set tested. merge-to-main.bpmn is where merging is a step with its own gate: it reads the head's evidence live (the train's green run is that evidence, and merge:guard re-evaluates it), establishes that the owner authorised THIS merge (explicitly, or by a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, e.g. 2026-10-01 "you may merge green PRs", which covers green heads only and only the queue as it stood), records the authorisation, merges pinned to the head, and then confirms main, re-pins downstream mounts and notes the bean. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. Each member's trainId is cleared, and its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. A member the sub-process does not merge (held, refused, handed back) leaves the train with its reason on its queue entry. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeToMain . Land it in library/ candidate, extracted A permanent sample joins the library as an L1 source, with the materialization record (purpose, gates, fixity) beside it. From here refresh-materialized governs it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Library . Land the bytes in the copier's own folio/ candidate, extracted Into the copier's own declared folio/, never a scratch area — a directory nobody declared is a directory nobody gates, and the copy would be publishable by accident. The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_Land . Land the feature's PRs candidate, extracted Phase 6's "explicit confirmation before merging to main", made a step that can refuse. Once per pull request the feature still has open, after the sign-off is recorded and before the issue is closed: an issue is not closed on a feature that is not on main. merge-to-main.bpmn reads each head's evidence live, establishes that the owner authorised THAT merge (a stakeholder sign-off or the BA's confirmation is acceptance of the feature, not authorisation to merge it, unless the owner's own words say so), records the authorisation, merges, and confirms the base. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. An increment the owner asked to land earlier in Phase 6 went through the same sub-process at that time. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process merge-to-main (Process_MergeToMain, sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). RESTORE: mount-from-lock replays the lock from refs/cat/layers/<key> (key = sha256 of the lock's layers), verifying every layer's tree digest, declaration and asset sha256 against the committed lock — class (a), verified against THIS tree, so a bad entry is only a miss, and a stale refs/cat/layers/main still serves every layer that did not move. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Layers . Lean .oleans: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 3, after the layers (the Lean packages are mounted content). RESTORE: the compiled .oleans of each declared Lean package, keyed by the package, the toolchain AND the lake manifest (the Mathlib revision) — the manifest is part of the key, so an entry from another revision is a miss. lake build re-checks every restored module's trace, so a stale module is rebuilt, not trusted: class (a). SAVE: main; a contributor's warm build may be offered back (compiled-artefact-cache) and is accepted only through that same trace check. Owner role: the integrator (CI speed 14). cache node: lean-oleans. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Lean . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_OfferWayBack . Leave it alone (coordinate instead) candidate, extracted Never resolve, scrap or delete a bean another session or a human owns. Claiming is how two sessions avoid picking the same item; closing someone else's is how one of them loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_LeaveAlone . Leave it as feedback candidate, extracted With no write tool the reader's point is not lost: it is recorded as feedback for someone who can write. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Todo . Leave it referenced, record why candidate, extracted A refusal is not a failure of the process — it is the process working. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Link the work to an issue candidate, extracted Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . List the locations this could install to candidate, extracted Zero or more. Is this a git repository already, or were one or more URLs to repositories supplied? Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListLocations . List the steps the declarations name candidate, extracted In the order of the table in initialization-steps: declaration, needs, each dependency's instructions, the documents at their IRIs (checked above; the report leads with them), directories, assets, README, README sections, site. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . List upstream releases and compare to the pin candidate, extracted git ls-remote --tags, filtered by the row's tagPattern and ordered by version. Nothing is cloned and no API token is needed, so the check runs the same way on a laptop and in CI. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#Task_QueryUpstream . Load or reuse the warm context candidate, extracted The validator's server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_ContextLoad . Load the active voices candidate, extracted The activated set only, never everything shipped. An id naming no shipped voice is an error rather than a skip — a folio that believes it is applying a voice and is applying nothing has the cleanest-looking output of the three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . Log a message or an error candidate, extracted Write a message or error entry whenever a later reader would need it. A command run goes in execution (command, exit code, where output went) — never the output itself, and never a secret, token or credential: capture on puts entries in git. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogMessage . Log findings on the bean candidate, extracted Validation failed: record the findings on the change's bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . Log findings on the bean candidate, extracted Findings are appended to the bean, so the next agent or human sees what is outstanding. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_LogFindings . Log task-end candidate, extracted Write a task-end entry, with the outcome in the detail. The step is the unit: an entry per step, not one when the whole process finishes, or every intermediate entry is lost. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogEnd . Log task-start candidate, extracted Write a task-start entry before touching anything: summary, actor, and the process/task/bean/branch/session it belongs to where they exist. role, process and task are optional on purpose — do not invent a lane for work done outside a process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_LogStart . Log the environment error on the bean candidate, extracted Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change's bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_LogEnvError . Log the failure candidate, extracted Every failure path passes through here, so "logged as failed" is a step somebody performs rather than an adjective on an end event. What differs between the ways in is the message, which is an input, not the mechanism. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogFailure . Log the start of the install candidate, extracted REQUIRED logging, which is what drawing the call says. Logged before anything is written, so an install interrupted halfway is distinguishable from one never begun. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogInstallStart .

6461.title: M
6461.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted The loop's only open-ended step. Everything around it is procedure; this is the work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Implement . Make the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_MakeChange . Make the change, check it and merge it candidate, extracted The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_MakeChange . Make the PR ready candidate, extracted Its own work is done and its full tier is green as judged; it is marked ready by the queue rule (continual-progress, Pace the ready marking). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Ready . Map the affected layers in order candidate, extracted Run the re-pin planner (mount:repin:cone) with the fleet and the changed repository. It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_MapCone . Map values onto palette roles candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . Mark it skip on the queue candidate, extracted Record on the queue file that the bean is held elsewhere, and by whom, so no other drainer takes it next. The bean itself is not touched: closing or noting on someone else's bean is how a sibling loses work it had not finished reporting. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-drain.bpmn#Drain_Skip . Mark the record superseded or retired candidate, extracted Never delete (git rm) a superseded or retired requirement. When superseding req:<old-slug>, set status: superseded and supersededBy: req:<new-slug> on docs/requirements/<old-slug>.md. When retiring, set status: retired and document the retirement reason and authorising issue in prose. Update any RequirementSet (docs/requirements/*.set.json) so approved/accepted sets hold only in-force members. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_UpdateLifecycle . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per layer, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge and publish candidate, extracted content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Publish . Merge each member onto the base candidate, extracted merge-base.bpmn once per member, in order, --no-regen; then ONE bun run cat regen over the result. Tool: merge:train. Always onto the current base, never a cached one (R5). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_MergeMembers . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge it through merge:guard candidate, extracted A workflow PR, or a PR in a repository with no train, merges directly. A workflow PR needs no approval beyond the batch card (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card Workflow PRs, A). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Task_Direct . Merge main in, regenerate, fix mechanical gates candidate, extracted Merge commits only; never a force-push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_AgentFix . Merge manager watch candidate, extracted The elected session holds the merge steward lane and runs its loop until it hands over or the lane lapses. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_CallWatch . Merge restored and rebuilt records candidate, extracted Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the base in, without committing candidate, extracted git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main on a clean tree (untracked files refuse too, so the final stage cannot sweep in a scratch file). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the layer's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . Merge the pull request candidate, extracted The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the re-pin with its decided revisions candidate, extracted The re-pin merges when its checks are green and every decision it needs is recorded. Its pull request cites the decisions, which become the release notes for this site's update. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge train candidate, extracted Add the merge-train label instead of merging; the train lands the batch with one CI run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Call_Train . Merge, hold or refuse candidate, extracted The owner's answer to the question Task_Ask asked. Their words are quoted verbatim in the record, so the answer is given in the conversation or on the PR, not inferred from tone. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_OwnerDecides . Merge, on explicit confirmation candidate, extracted The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge, pinned to the evaluated head candidate, extracted Through merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <id> where the repository has it; elsewhere with the merge call pinned to the head SHA, so GitHub refuses if the head moved. Merge commit unless the repository or owner says otherwise. Never delete the branch. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mirror it to the feedback channel candidate, extracted Review sheet: the "Decision needed" block in the row's agent column, Agentic status Needs you (the document layer's review-sheet-script skill). Issue or PR: a comment. An extra copy, never instead of the discussion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Mirror . Mount each layer at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the layer's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. A replay of the lock tries the index's layers cache ref first (refs/cat/layers/<key>, then refs/cat/layers/main): one shallow fetch, every byte verified against the lock, and any layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source: another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-prepare.bpmn#Task_Hosted . Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move it into its repositories candidate, extracted Create the repositories, drain, seed, consume additively, release, and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Move . Move it into its repository candidate, extracted Create the repository, drain, copy the staged contents in, re-point the declaration, verify a fresh clone, then consume, release and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Move . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin . Move the pin and open the PR candidate, extracted The pin literal moves in the one file upstream-pins.json declares, and the PR body says what the version range changed in RENDERED output — the evidence, not just the verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_ApplyPin . MVP: build the candidate on a staging branch candidate, extracted An MVP is a DEPLOYED BUILD, not a description of one. The pin is moved on a branch and feature-staging.yml publishes it under branches/<branch-slug>/, so the reviewer looks at the artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Mvp .

6462.title: N
6462.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library's image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, "Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . Narrative review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeReview. The actor takes on the narrative-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview . No CI: run the repo's own gates locally candidate, extracted Only on no-ci. Run the repository's own gates (its tests, typecheck and whatever its README or package.json names) on the merge result, not the branch. Record each command, exit code and the SHA it ran on. This is evidence the owner can weigh. It is not CI, and the question to the owner says so in words. 6463.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. Place it in uploads/ by a declared route candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is "Contributor (human or agent)" because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. 6465.title: Q
6465.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA report and one PR to main candidate, extracted Write each locale's QA report, then open one PR for the layer, based on and targeting main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Report . QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_QaWorkingCopy . BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_QcGates . 6505.title: SMART Trust HCERT library tools
6505.content: Requirements and contracts for the SMART Trust HCERT API libraries: Kotlin first (JVM, Android, Node), Rust second (WebAssembly). They are derived from the WHO SMART Trust implementation guide, in particular the QR Code Generation page of WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#129.

6510.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
6510.title: Lanes — who acts
6510.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Writes four records in a fixed order, then reads the source’s glossary and reference lists into the KG, and touches the corpus graph in none of them — dublin-core as the record of truth, a manifest that references it, assets[] kept as a SIBLING of library: because that tree is regenerated and would drop anything written inside it, and finally the slug binding Task_Link depends on. A wrong order or placement is invisible until the next sync drops it. | .

6511.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
6511.title: Steps
6511.content: Every one of the 7 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write dublin-core.jsonld (the record of truth)Task_Dublin | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus’s JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one. | . | Write manifest.jsonld referencing itTask_Manifest | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields. | . | Record assets[] — local path or remote URLTask_Assets | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Extract reference listsTask_References | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Each reference list of the source (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section, in any of the six UN languages) becomes folio-reference/v1 nodes with the Tool references-extract: one node per cited work, provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section it was read from, and printed the entry exactly as the source prints it. Only fields read without guessing are set (address, DOI, ISBN, year, access date); a cited IRIS item the library holds gets heldAt. The nodes are the document’s own bibliography on the bibliography page. A source with no reference list skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

6516.doc: Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets
6516.title: Steps
6516.content: Every one of the 8 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Archive → greppable contents manifestTask_Archive | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. | . | File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetypeTask_TechMeta | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. | . | Narrative description per image, localizedTask_Image | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library’s image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Transcribe and translate audioTask_Audio | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | No Tool yet; the method, and the choice of recogniser, is skill audio-transcription. | . | Sheet names, headers, shape, narrativeTask_Tabular | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Tools tabular-csv and tabular-xlsx, as CSVW (skill tabular-metadata). CSV and spreadsheet: tabs, column and row headers, sizes, and what the dataset is about. | . | Extract figures and tablesTask_FiguresTables | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The pdf-images.py, pdf-vector-labels.py and pdf-vector-figures.py arms extract the raster images and the figures drawn as vectors (grouped and rendered). For every table the document’s structure declares, an agent reads the rendered page, checks cell text against the text layer, and writes tables/<label>.csv plus tables.csvw.json (folio-tabular-csvw/v1), with a draft description in the six UN languages; pdf-tables.py’s grid is a cross-check, not the answer. Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris): “actually extract the figures” and “any tables too”. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Footnotes and the marks that call themTask_Footnotes | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | The pdf-footnotes.py arm (owner, 2026-11-11, “also foot notes/marks”): from the page layout, each note at the foot of a page and every superscript mark in the text that calls it, written to footnotes.json (folio-document-footnotes/v1) with the block that holds the page. The section text is not changed. Only a called note is a footnote; uncalled foot-of-page lines and marks with no note are listed, never dropped. OCR’d pages have no fonts and are reported unread. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “Footnotes and their marks”. | . | Cite the author of every narrativeTask_Provenance | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source. | .

6520.title: Lanes — who acts
6520.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Two provenance paths converge on the same Task_Sections output — an embedded text layer extracted directly, or OCR that leaves the fuller text in ocr/ with only a stub in sections/ — and which branch this lane took is invisible downstream except to a grep that knows to check the fourth tier. Task_Candidates stays a proposal: nothing downstream may treat it as an adjudicated verdict. | .

6521.title: Steps
6521.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | Check each page; OCR pages that failTask_PageCheck | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris, card Q-ODD-1 = A): “force OCR when a page’s text layer fails a quality check”. A text layer can hold plenty of letters and still not be the page’s text: accents mapped to Greek letters (“dΘclaration”), Persian set in the wrong Arabic code points, words split by kerning (“au g m ente”), fake-bold words printed twice, mojibake. cat-harness-tools scripts/_text_quality.py checks every page against the document’s languages (dc.language.iso, or –lang-hint); the router then OCRs the document and pdf-structure.py –ocr takes the OCR text for the failing pages only, listing them in structure.json source.ocr_pages with the reason. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “A text layer that is not text”. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Each page is read in the document’s languages (–lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article’s Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document’s references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. An outline is set aside when its entries are machine bookmark names (_GoBack, _Hlk…, “Blank Page”, a merged file’s name) or when under half of them name a heading the pages print, and the contents are inferred instead (diagnostics.outline_rejected). A section that would hold more than half of a document of 20 pages or more (and over 8,000 words), or over 20,000 words anywhere, is cut at the headings inferred inside it, else one section per page (diagnostics.oversized_split). Owner, 2026-11-11: “split single blocks that hold a whole book”. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “An outline that is not contents, and a section too long to be a block”. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256.
