A cancelled job counts only when a later run of the same workflow on the same head SHA passed the matching job (concurrency supersession). Merge with expectedHeadSha set to the full 40-hex head SHA, never a short one. | Standing OK. An owner instruction such as “merge everything green” is an explicit OK for every PR that meets rule 1, until the owner withdraws it. Merges still follow any stated chain order: a later PR in a chain waits for the earlier one. | One PR per fix. Before opening a fix or re-pin PR, search the open PRs in that repository for the same files. If one exists, compare the diffs and coordinate instead. If a duplicate is found later, the author of the later PR closes it, after checking that the diffs are identical. While main is red, one session owns the re-pin that fixes it, and says so to the merge-planning session. | A re-pin is a cross-layer set. Find every layer the change needs, a main-red fix or any other, and pin them together in one re-pin, to the current mains. Pins move only forward. Verify on a fresh mount (mount:remote --fresh). A stale container mount gives false local passes. The rules and an example are in remote-mount §”Re-pinning” (owner rulings, 2026-11-06, card “Pin target”, A, and 2026-11-07). | Hand back private caches. A PR that adds its own cache scheme instead of the shared cached-step is held, not merged, and goes back to its author. Cache-first CI, rule 1: every cache goes through cached-step. | Tabulation can be delegated. A helper agent may tabulate the sweep under these rules. The helper never touches the PRs the steward owns, and never pushes, comments or closes. | The train’s PRs are the train’s. A PR labelled merge-train or merge-train-batch is landed by the merge train only, in a batch with one main move and one main CI run. The sweep skips it, as merge-main.yml does; every other PR that meets rule 1 merges as before. A sweep that merges a labelled PR one at a time starves the train (owner ruling, 2026-11-06: “1. The train”). | Approved PRs go through the train (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Train”, A). When the owner approves a folio-assistant PR that does not change .github/workflows/, the merge manager adds the merge-train label instead of merging it. The train lands a batch with one CI run. Merging one PR at a time cost about 6.7 runs per merged PR. A PR that changes workflows, and a PR in a repository with no train, merges directly. | Stacks merge bottom-up (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). A PR whose body says stacked on <repo>#<n> waits for that PR. The merge manager lands the base first, the stacked PR’s owner retargets it onto main and merges main in, and only then does it count as ready. A stacked folio-assistant PR gets the merge-train label only after it has been retargeted to main. A cross-layer stack waits until its pin names the dependency’s merge commit on main. The merge request lists the order, and the batch card keeps it. | A re-pin PR holds only pins (owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “keep repins on own PR so easier to stack dependencies”). When the sweep finds a re-pin PR (one that changes index.config.json or index.lock.json) that also carries a feature, workflow logic or a fix, the merge manager does not land it. It sends it back, and asks for the extra change to be split onto a PR stacked on the re-pin, or into the layer that owns the fix. Counter-example: folio-assistant#2985 carried #2999 and a caches:viz gate line inside its re-pin. Exception (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “A. Allow the exception”): a change mutually dependent with the re-pin, where neither passes alone, may share the PR when its body says why (as a content layer’s re-pin did on 2026-11-07). The merge manager checks the reason; a change that only needs the new pins still stacks. | .

6882.title: Runner relief
6882.content: The merge manager enforces the pacing rule of continual-progress §”Pace the ready marking” (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Cancel CI”). When the runners are saturated, it: . | closes superseded or duplicate PRs, such as a re-pin whose commits another open PR already carries, and cancels their runs; | cancels stale queued runs that never started, but never a main push run that has started; | asks the owners of P3 PRs to return them to draft. | .

6883.title: Keeping the swarm in step
6883.content: . | Hold. Before any batch landing (a train or a meta-merge), message every sibling that pushes to the repositories involved: what is about to land, and “hold pushes, merges and run cancels here until done”. | Done. After the landing, post “done” with what landed and what is still open. Post it even when the owner chose not to go ahead. A hold with no “done” is an outage. | Hand back. A PR that cannot land (conflict, protected path, red) goes back to its owner with the reason, on the PR’s own thread or work item. It is never fixed inside the train. | Report. After every landing, report to the owner: what merged, the main verdict on each repository, and any open decision. Keep it to one message. | .

6884.title: Safety rules (STRICT)
6884.content: These come from the role; the watcher is the step that acts on them: . | Only the merge manager merges, in any repository, and a scheduled routine never merges (§”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”). | Merges happen only on the owner’s explicit OK, given in the merge manager’s session. A tap on the batch card counts, and the card names each PR. A standing OK counts for the PRs it covers (rule 2). A sibling’s or coordinator’s request does not count, and neither does an approval the owner gave in a sibling’s session. | Leave every PR labelled content out of the status table and the batch cards (owner, 2026-11-15). merge:watch already skips them. Content goes to the owner one by one, on its documented review (prepare-merge §”Content PRs”). | Never merge committee content, change sets (CS-), or held subscriptions/ trees. Never touch WHO or smart-* upstream repositories. | Never push .github/workflows/ changes without the workflows permission. | Never cancel a main push run that has already started. | Never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get to green. | .

6885.title: What this does not do yet
6885.content: . | merge:guard check 3 (ready-marker) still asks for a ready: <sha> comment signed by the PR’s own session. That still works: a session may post the marker on its own PR, and then sends the six lines to the merge manager. What it cannot cover is a PR whose session can neither post nor reach GitHub, because nobody else may post the marker for it (rule 1). Follow-up for the tools layer (owner, 2026-11-13: “update process and tools”): . | check 3 accepts the ready-to-merge label, alone or with a pinned head, in place of the ready: comment, so sessions stop posting ready comments; | merge:watch lists the PRs labelled ready-to-merge and needs-repin as the merge manager’s queue, each with its CI verdict; | every merge path (merge:guard --merge) says that only the merge manager runs it, and a standing re-pin run opens a needs-repin PR and never merges (card “C. No auto-merge”); | a workflow posts the merge-guard status, so that it can be required on main (card “A. merge-guard required status”); | --no-merge-manager is renamed to say what it now means: the merge manager landing a PR of its own. | . | The needs-repin label must exist in each repository the merge manager watches before an agent can use it. | The timer is each session’s own scheduled check-in. No workflow wakes the merge manager yet. | .

6886.title: merge-manager-watcher (skill)
6886.content: The skill merge-manager-watcher as its source file cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/merge-manager-watcher.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

6887.title: Merge queue — what lands next, and as what
6887.content: Skill merge-queue: Order the ready PRs and land them as a train: read each PR’s live facts, let the reprioritisation table place it, merge the members together, run the gate set on the combination, and on red attribute and eject the culprit rather than reject the train. Every merge goes through merge:guard. Use for “merge the ready PRs”, “land this PR”, “what lands next”, “run a merge train”, “why was my PR ejected”, “move this PR up”, and when tuning the train’s order or size. Named by: Merge manager watch: wake, read the queue live, route, Merge to main, A merge train, Saturation meta-merge: land the ready PRs when the runners are full, Guideline Updates . sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn is the process. The ORDER is computed by sdlc/processes/decisions/merge-priority.dmn; the facts it reads are derived by scripts/merge-queue.ts; what the steward decided is recorded against schemas/sdlc/merge-queue.ts. This page says what each piece is FOR.

6888.title: The rule everything else follows from
6888.content: The queue stores decisions, never GitHub’s facts. CI status, mergeability, labels and head SHA change without the queue being told, so a stored copy is stale the moment it is written and a reader cannot tell which. They are read live at each step. What a queue entry holds is what the steward DECIDED — the placement, a hold, an ejection — with who decided it, when, and the evidence URL it acted on. FORBIDDEN_FACT_KEYS in the schema refuses an entry that carries a fact.

6889.title: What “ready to merge” means (STRICT)
6889.content: Owner, 2026-11-15: “clarify what ready to merge means (e.g. Ready, green PRs, CI passes etc. need generic ready and cat-harness specific processes)”. Two layers: a generic definition for any repository, and what a cat-harness layer adds on top of it. Generic: any repository . A PR is ready to merge when all of these hold: . | Out of draft: its author marked it ready for review. | No conflicts with its base branch. | CI passes: every required check on its head has finished and is green, judged against the repository’s own dependencies. A red that also fails on the base branch’s own main, and that the PR does not cause, does not block it; the PR says so, and that red has someone fixing it. | Its description is complete: what it changes and why, how it was verified, and no unticked checklist item. | Every approval it needs is given: any review the repository requires, and any owner decision the change depends on. | . A ready PR merges right away, in the same pass, lowest dependency first. It does not wait for a batch, for a later PR, or for anything in a repository that depends on it. cat-harness layers: in addition . Every repository built on cat-harness (the harness, its tools, the content layers and the index) adds these to the generic list: . | The content rule. A PR labelled content is ready only when the owner has asked to review it and its ## Content review section names the review record (prepare-merge §”Content PRs”). It merges on the owner’s approval, never from the queue. Every other PR is non-content and goes through the queue. | The hand-over. Its own session marked it ready and labelled it ready-to-merge (or needs-repin when only a re-pin is missing), or sent the merge manager its request (merge-manager-watcher §”The merge request: six lines”). Only the merge manager merges. | merge:guard passes: base, ready-for-review, ready marker, labels, CI, checklist, open question, mergeable, and content review. The merge-guard commit status is success. Where the guard and this list disagree, fix the guard. | Linked to its issue, with a comment on that issue for each push. | Pins. A PR that changes index.lock.json (a re-pin or an integration PR) moves each pinned layer to that layer’s current main, with the pins agreeing with each other, and needs the full tier green on its head, not only the fast tier. Any other PR is judged against its own layer’s pins, never a dependent’s (§”A lower repository never waits on a higher one”). | .

6890.title: A lower repository never waits on a higher one (STRICT)
6890.content: Owner, 2026-11-15: “A lower layer never waits on a higher one”. A PR in a repository is judged only against the repositories it depends on: . | Merging: a lower repository’s PR is never held for a dependent’s lock, pins, train or red main. A dependent catches up through its own re-pin. | CI design: each repository’s checks run against its own dependencies at the versions it pins, never against a dependent’s pins of it. A gate that mounts a dependent’s index and therefore tests an older copy of the repository under review is a defect in that gate: file it, and do not let its red block the PR (generic rule 3 above). | Fixes flow up: when a lower change breaks a dependent, the fix lands in the dependent (or in the lower repository, if it is the lower one’s bug) after the lower PR merges; the lower PR is not reverted for it unless its own main is red. | .

6891.title: Handing a PR to the queue — the sibling session’s side (STRICT)
6891.content: merge-train.bpmn has two lanes that matter here: . | sibling-session (“Sibling session”): whoever submits a PR to the queue and fixes it when it is handed back. | merge-steward (“Merge steward”): whoever orders and lands the queue. | . Both are ROLES, not sessions, so nothing in this section depends on which session holds either lane. The PR is the message . The steward reads open PRs labelled ready-to-merge, and nothing else. A PR labelled content is never in the queue, even with ready-to-merge on it: it waits for the owner on its documented content review (prepare-merge §”Content PRs”). A comment posted anywhere else reaches nobody: not on a PR you believe is the steward’s, and not on an issue. A session that cannot message the merge manager labels its own PR instead: ready-to-merge when it is green, needs-repin when it is green except for a re-pin. Only the merge manager acts on either label (merge-manager-watcher §”The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first”; owner, 2026-11-13). Ask the user before submitting . When you finish your work and are ready to merge, ask the user before submitting to the merge queue. Do not apply ready-to-merge or post the ready: marker autonomously without asking the user if you should submit. Submitting to the queue requests landing the code on main; the user or owner confirms the submission. While a merge manager is active, tell it, and never merge yourself . Owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Approvals”, B: siblings send merge requests to the merge manager, and the owner approves only in the merge manager’s session. So, besides the steps below, send the merge manager the six-line merge request: the PR URL and full head SHA, your session URL, what changed, the rendered preview URL (or no preview: <reason>), what to look for in it, and full tier green as judged. A request with no preview and no reason comes back. Never merge your own PR. An approval the owner gives in your session does not authorise a merge. The merge manager posts your request in its chat, asks the owner on its batch card, and orders the queue: merge-manager-watcher §”Am I the active merge manager?” and §”The merge request: six lines”. Find the merge manager before you send: the latest merge manager: <session id> announcement, noted on the coordination work item, names a session that must also be live. When none is active the siblings elect one by a fixed rule; a lone session is elected alone; the lane never lapses into self-merging (owner ruling, 2026-11-13); and one that does not acknowledge within the stall window is treated as stalled (merge-manager-watcher §”The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first”). Submitting to the queue . To submit, do all of these on YOUR PR: . | Owed CI is green on the head, for a release. See §”Admission asks which runs are OWED”. On a non-release merge CI is advisory (owner, card Q-CIB-4 A, 2026-11-08): it is read and reported, and it does not hold the PR (merge-to-main §”CI gates a release only”). | The PR is ready for review, not a draft. | It carries the label ready-to-merge. | It has a comment ready: <full head sha>, signed with your session link (https://claude.ai/code/session_…). Every session acts with the owner’s token, so the link is the only thing that tells sessions apart. A _Generated by Claude Code_ footer alone is not a signature. | It does not carry needs-merge-human. merge-main.yml adds that label when it refuses a merge and never removes it. If you have since merged main by hand, remove the label, and say why in a comment. | The body has no unticked box, and there is no open question to the owner or the steward. | An agent-touched PR has an adversarial review on its head, recorded on the merge-reviews state branch by a session that is not the author (adversarial-code-review). The gate is warn-only for now, so a missing verdict is reported, not refused. A train keeps each PR’s verdict, because the review is per head. | . Watch status after submitting — never fire-and-forget . When you submit something to the merge queue, you need to watch what its status is. Submitting is not the end of your turn. Watch the GitHub Actions runs on the head (check:head-has-run), evaluate merge-guard, and monitor whether the PR is admitted into a train or whether it is refused, held, or failing checks. If CI fails, diagnose and repair the failure immediately rather than leaving a failing PR in the queue. Merge order goes on the PR, and setting an order is the owner’s call. | Write it in the ready: comment, on every PR it concerns (“merge before #N”). | Quote the owner’s ruling with its date. | When two PRs must not land in the wrong order, keep the label OFF the later one until the earlier one lands. A label is the only hold the steward is certain to see. | . After submitting: do not spend CI you do not need yet . Once CI has confirmed the PR, a submitter far back in the queue should not burn CI cycles keeping up with a churning main. Every merge of main into your PR re-runs the whole suite. While other PRs are landing, each of those runs is obsolete before the steward reaches you. | The first green is what admits you. Your ready: marker stays valid across merge-main bot merges (see “A push makes the marker stale” below), so the steward can still see a PR that is a few merges behind. | Far back, stand still. If your PR is not in the next train or two (the steward’s status comment on your PR gives your position), do not merge main by hand to stay current. Take merge-main off as well: that label makes the bot merge main into your PR on every push to main (§”Your merge cadence is an input to the bot’s throughput”). | Near the front, catch up once. When you are in the next train, or the steward asks you to: . | put merge-main back on, or merge main by hand (prepare-merge §”Submodules: check the pointers BEFORE you stage the merge”); | let CI go green; | post a fresh signed ready:. | . | A conflict is the exception. If main now conflicts with your PR, fix it when you see it, wherever you are in the queue. A conflict is work, not churn. | . A push makes the marker stale. A head newer than your ready: sha is not intake, unless every commit since is a merge-main bot merge. Post ready: again for the new head once CI is green on it. Do not post “ready soon”: it is not intake, and it costs the steward a read. The steward’s side: reach a submitter who has fallen behind . While watching the queue, and after every reshuffle or disentangling of trains, the steward checks the PRs near the front. A PR there can be: . | behind main and conflicted; | red, or with an owed run missing on its head; | carrying a stale ready:; | carrying needs-merge-human. | . When the steward finds one, it tells the submitter. It never fixes the PR on the submitter’s behalf, and never waits in silence. It uses the skills it already has: . | The status comment on the PR, edited in place. It states the position, what is missing, and by when. Its shape is the one in merge-conflict-patterns §”When a merge-train member is refused”. | A hand-back work item when the PR is ejected or handed back (same section). The submitting role picks it up even if the original session is gone. Every hand-back gets one, not only a train ejection. That covers Rule_Refused, Rule_HeadNotGreen, Rule_NotReady, and a merge:guard refusal on a PR the owner asked to land. A PR comment and a queue entry are not a hand-back on their own: the work plan cannot see them. | Shape: titled Merge refused: #<n> <cause>, type: bug, parented under the PR’s work item’s parent (or under the PR’s work item when it is an epic or feature), marked --blocking that work item. | Body: the refused checks, roles, the brief (link the takeover plan if there is one), where to report, Done when, and Fails if. | Dedupe: check first, because beans create dedupes on nothing. | Process: run it through sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn (workflow_start), not from memory. | . merge:steward prints ✗ handed back with NO open hand-back bean: #… and carries handBackBean per PR in --json, because a procedure that lives in another skill is skipped unless something checks for it. | A direct message as the fast path, by the recipe below. Use it when the PR is next and waiting costs a train. | The queue entry records the hold or ejection, with its reason and expiry (§”The steward answers in the queue”). | . A submitter told “you are next” catches up at once. That is the trade this section makes: CI is spent on the PRs about to land, not on the whole queue. Address the ROLE, never a session . The Merge Steward is a lane in merge-train.bpmn, not a particular session, and whoever holds it today may not hold it tomorrow. So the handover must not depend on who that is: . | no session id written anywhere, since it dies with its container; | no “they are active on PR #N”, since that PR may merge or the role may move; | no message as the channel. | . Whoever takes the lane next reads the same open PRs and the same queue entries. A direct message is a fast path on top of that, never a replacement. Use one when it is the more efficient tool, and say how you used it. It saves the receiver a polling cycle, but it never counts as handing over: the PR’s own state still has to say ready. The same recipe works in both directions: . | Find whoever holds the other role now. Do not use a remembered session id. | Cloud: run list_sessions (claude-code-remote). Match the session whose title or external_metadata.current_branches shows the lane, or the PR’s head branch when you are looking for a submitter. | Same machine: run ListAgents. | . | Check it can receive. For a cloud session, run get_session(id) and confirm cross_session_inbound == "available". | Send one line. Use send_message (cloud) or SendMessage (same machine), naming the PR and the head sha. The PR comment stays the record; the message only points at it. | If any step fails, stop. Do not post the message as a comment on some other PR or issue instead. | . coordinate §”What actually reaches a sibling” has the measurements of which tool reaches which kind of session. The steward answers in the queue, and the queue lives on the beans branch . Once the steward has decided something about your PR (a placement, a hold, an ejection), that decision is an entry under beans/queue/<pr>.json. The entry carries pr and beans, the work items and epics the PR serves; name them in your PR body so the steward can copy them. That list is the association between a PR and its work items. Where to read it depends on the state-branch cutover. The queue is moving to its OWN branch, cat/cat-harness/merge-queue — §”Where the queue is GOING” below — and where the two disagree, that section governs: . | Before the cutover, main is authoritative. Entries reach it only through the steward’s own PRs, a PR cycle late, so the edited-in-place status comment on your PR is the live answer. | After the cutover, beans/ (with queue/ inside it) is authoritative on the orphan branch cat/cat-harness/beans. Read it with bun run cat state:mount. The steward writes an entry the moment it decides, then bun run cat state:push, which splices only the changed paths onto the tip and stops on a conflicting write instead of overwriting it. The entry is then live for everyone, and the status comment is a courtesy that points at it. | . The branch’s manifest.json says which state it is in ("authoritative"). Read that rather than this paragraph. The cutover also changes what a work item can do here. A work item created on a code branch is invisible until the PR lands; a work item written through state:push is visible at once. A submitter can then note on the PR’s work item that it is submitted, and the steward can answer on the same work item. The PR state above stays the intake signal either way: the work item is where the conversation is kept. Not GitHub’s merge queue. It is not offered on a personal-account repository. The merge guard (bun run cat merge:guard <pr>) checks the six submission points mechanically; run it against your own PR before you announce.

6892.title: Where the queue is GOING, and the tool that will write it
6892.content: Not cut over yet. The queue is still on main under beans/queue/. The store and CLI below exist; the cutover to its own branch, cat/cat-harness/merge-queue, is a separate small change during which the steward pauses queue writes. Until it lands, merge:queue:read reads the checkout and merge:queue:record refuses — keep committing entries to main as §”The steward answers in the queue” describes. The branch’s manifest.json says which state it is in. Why the queue comes off main at all is structural: an entry on main arrives only through a pull request, and the steward does no development work — it must not open PRs of its own, which would have it setting its own priority in the queue it manages, spending the CI the queue is starved of, and judging its own head. On main, the one actor whose decisions the queue records is the one actor that cannot write to it. After the cutover: . bun run cat state:mount # the queue on disk at its declared path bun run cat merge:queue:read # the recorded decisions bun run cat merge:queue:record --pr <n> --class <c> --rank <r> --rule <id> \ --reason "<why>" --by <your session URL> # ...or --position <n> for an owner override . | record pushes by default, as a splice onto the branch tip carrying the blob each file was read at. So the entry is live for every sibling at once, and a steward who edited the same entry since gets this write stopped as a conflict with the path named rather than overwritten. On a conflict, re-mount and decide again; nothing was pushed and the local edit is the only copy. --no-push leaves it in the mount, where nobody else can see it. | --reason and --by are required. A placement nobody can explain cannot be honoured or safely undone by the next steward, and every session here acts with the owner’s token, so the session link is the only thing that says which steward decided. | An unreachable queue is not an empty one. merge:queue:read exits 4 and readQueueEntries THROWS when the branch is not mounted, because “no decisions recorded, all clear” printed over a graph nobody read is a false clean. Exit 1 — declared-but-absent — is a different answer with a different remedy. | The decisions are read back. merge:steward feeds recorded overrides into the table’s ownerOverride input and their positions into the order, treats an un-cleared ejection as refused, and prints a live hold, because a decision nobody reads back is a decision nobody took. | . The queue’s decisions and a finished train run’s evidence (under workflows/) live in different stores, one state:mount apart. The trade is deliberate: kept together on main, the queue could hold no entry the steward wrote.

6893.title: Placement is computed, not chosen
6893.content: GW_Placement is DMN-backed, so workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome there. The table (hit policy FIRST) answers a route (admit or hand back), a class (PRIORITY_CLASSES), a rank and whether the PR rides alone. | An owner override is an INPUT (ownerOverride), never an outcome. The owner places a PR by hand in Task_Override; the schema refuses an override placement without a reason. | Independence is decided on AUTHORED paths (authoredPaths, touchesShared). Generated paths are excluded because merge-conflict-patterns already resolves them; counting them would make every pair of PRs conflict. | Ties go to the oldest PR (orderQueue): overrides at their positions, then rank, then PR number. | .

6894.title: Admission asks which runs are OWED, never whether anything is red
6894.content: On a release, a member is admitted on ownCi == "green" (on a non-release merge ownCi is reported, not required; owner, card Q-CIB-4 A, 2026-11-08), and green means every workflow owed for the head’s event ran and succeeded. It does not mean “nothing is failing”. A head can have every expected job name present, no failure anywhere, and still have runs in_progress and suites completed with conclusion: action_required that executed nothing. Counting the runs does not catch it. Only asking which runs are owed for this event catches it, and check-head-has-run is the one thing here that asks. Do not write a second checker: it already keeps the states apart, has a test, and is already wired into pr-checks-present.bpmn. Its five states are the five values of ownCi, and collapsing any two is the defect: . | value | means | . | green | every owed run present and successful — the only admitting value | . | red | an owed run ran and failed | . | missing-required | it HAS runs, but not the ones owed | . | none | GitHub answered and nothing names this head | . | unknown | could not ask: no network, rate limit, HTTP error | . unknown is handed back, never admitted and never reported as red: telling somebody their head is unverified when you merely could not look trains them to ignore the signal, which costs more than the gap. This is a gate, not advice. Rule_HeadNotGreen in merge-priority.dmn sits immediately after Rule_Refused under hitPolicy="FIRST", so anything but green routes to hand-back before any admitting rule can fire, and workflow_gate refuses a hand-supplied outcome. A dispatch is not an owed run. workflow_dispatch is the designed workaround for the bot-actor push condition (merge-main.yml dispatches the gating workflows for exactly that reason), but a dispatched run is evidence about the TREE, not evidence that the owed pull_request run exists. Report the two facts separately.

6895.title: Overlap has a KIND, and a train is the right answer to one of the four
6895.content: conflictRisk answers is there a collision. A steward needs is it the kind a train is for, which is overlapKind: . | kind | means | what it needs | . | none | no path shared with any live member | nothing | . | generated-only | shares paths, every one resolved by a declared pattern | regeneration | . | shared-declaration | the only authored paths shared are shared declarations | ordering | . | authored | shares an authored path that is not a declaration | a train | . Four values rather than three because a shared declaration is a subset of an authored path, not a sibling: classify("package.json").strategy is refuse, so it is authored, and isSharedDeclaration("package.json") is true. A three-value partition would file a declaration-only collision under authored and build trains nobody needed. authored outranks shared-declaration, which outranks generated-only, because at each step the earlier kind is the one the later kind’s remedy cannot resolve. The partition is tested in scripts/tests/merge-queue.test.ts — including that a refused member cannot be the other side of a collision, since it never enters a train.

6896.title: A train admits only members that STACK cleanly (STRICT)
6896.content: A train is a stack: member n+1 merges onto main + members 1…n with no conflict at all, generated paths included, and with no semantic break (tsc and the gate set pass on the stack). Check every candidate before admitting it: . c=origin/main for p in <members in order>; do t=$(git merge-tree --write-tree $c pr/$p) || { echo "#$p does not stack"; break; } c=$(git commit-tree $t -p $c -p pr/$p -m stack) done . A member that does not stack is not admitted. It does not go in on the promise that merge:main will resolve it. It goes back to its own session, which merges main on its own branch, gets CI green, and re-signals. Conflict resolution belongs on the member’s branch, never in the train, and never in the steward’s time. Resolving conflicts inside a train blocks everything else from landing. The overlapKind table above still says what a collision NEEDS; the steward provides only the none row. Every other kind goes back to its owner.

6897.title: The automated merge train (folio-assistant, work item folio-assistant-hd58)
6897.content: Where a repository runs merge-train.yml, as it does in folio-assistant, the steward’s hand train is a workflow. A person opts a PR in by adding the merge-train label (a bot’s label does not count) or by approving it. Every 15 minutes, when there is work, the train: . | judges the open train PR (merge-train-batch) as the re-pin train is judged: every check finished, the full tier ran, and no check fails that passes on main, check by check. When green, it merges the train PR with a merge commit, and every member is then on main; | on red, ejects a batch of one (label removed, failures listed), or splits a larger batch in halves and tests the first half next (about log₂ k extra runs for one culprit); | otherwise stacks the ready opted-in PRs on main with merge:train (in folio-assistant) and opens ONE train PR, which CI judges once. | . Owner ruling, 2026-11-05 (“Resolve generated only”). For the automated train this supersedes §”A train admits only members that STACK cleanly” for GENERATED paths only. A conflict that a declared generated-path pattern covers is resolved mechanically at train time and proved by the candidate’s CI. A conflict in any hand-written file ejects that PR with a comment, and it waits for its author. No person resolves conflicts in the train. Owner ruling, 2026-11-05 (off switch). A PR that changes .github/workflows/ rides the train only when the repository variable MERGE_TRAIN_CARRIES_WORKFLOWS is true and a bot token with the workflows permission is present. Until then, workflow PRs are merged one at a time when green (owner, 2026-11-05, option 1). subscriptions/ never rides. merge-main.yml skips PRs labelled merge-train: they are integrated once, at train time, never on each push to main. Owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Train”, A. When the owner approves a folio-assistant PR that does not change .github/workflows/, the merge manager adds the merge-train label instead of merging it, so the train lands it in a batch with one CI run. Merging one PR at a time cost about 6.7 runs per merged PR. Workflow PRs, and repositories with no train, merge directly, and a workflow PR needs no approval beyond the batch card (card “Workflow PRs”, A).

6898.title: Regenerate on a clean tree, and check it
6898.content: git status --porcelain is empty before a member is merged and the tree regenerated. Checked, not assumed, on Task_Admit. Generated directory READMEs carry a per-subdirectory file count, and the writer counts the files git would commit — git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard (bootstrap-tools/scripts/git-files.ts:23). --exclude-standard keeps ignored junk out, which is the __pycache__ case that drove that line, but --others still counts an untracked file nobody has ignored. So a transient written by an earlier train step moves a committed count, readme:subgraphs:check goes red, and the red belongs to nobody. The precondition does not make the count stable: two members each adding a file still write different integers to one line. merge:main resolves them under readme-generated-regions; a merge made by plain git does not. Not -merge and not a merge driver — both are refused in .gitattributes, the first because it tidies conflicts without removing them and the second because it needs per-checkout git config.

6899.title: A red train ejects one member, not the train
6899.content: . | Retry only a declared-flaky gate, and only once (Task_RetryFlaky). A deterministic gate retried learns nothing. | Attribute from each member’s own CI first (Task_Attribute). A member whose own CI is red, or never ran on its head — GitHub runs no pull_request CI while a PR conflicts — is the prime suspect, at no cost. | Bisect only when every member is green alone (Task_Bisect). | Eject and hand back with the reason (Task_Eject, then merge-refusal.bpmn). The ejection is written on the member’s entry; the rest re-run without it. The owning session fixes and re-signals ready; it is never merged on its behalf. | .

6900.title: A PR lands only through merge:guard (STRICT)
6900.content: Every merge a steward makes goes through bun run cat merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <your session id>. Never gh api -X PUT …/pulls/<n>/merge, never the web button, never merge_pull_request from an MCP tool, and, while a Merge Manager is active, never by marking a PR ready or labelling it yourself first (with none active, see §”When no Merge Manager is active”). The script (cat-harness-tools/scripts/merge-guard.ts) is the merge: it evaluates eight checks over GitHub’s live facts, and performs the PUT, pinned to the head it evaluated, only when every one passes. A direct PUT lands a PR whatever its state. When no Merge Manager is active, elect one; only it merges . Owner ruling, 2026-11-13: only the merge manager merges (merge-manager-watcher §”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”). With none active, the siblings elect one first, and a lone session is elected alone. A PR’s own session lands its PR only when it is that merge manager, once the owner has said to merge, and still through the guard: . bun run cat merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <your session id> --no-merge-manager . --no-merge-manager lifts one thing: check 2’s refusal of a merging session that marked the PR ready itself. Every other check still applies, and so does check 2’s own-session attribution. In particular, the ready: <head sha> marker signed by this session, ready-to-merge, green owed CI and a clean merge are all still required. The verdict says the separation was lifted, so the landing is auditable. Where the guard cannot run (for example a cloud sandbox whose gh has no usable token), do not merge: hand the landing to a session that can run it, or ask the owner. No workflow posts a merge-guard commit status, so there is no posted verdict to read in its place. How to tell whether a Merge Manager is active: the owner says so, or a live session holds the merge-steward lane (§”Address the ROLE, never a session”, step 1). If you cannot tell, apply the rules of merge-manager-watcher §”The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first”: with none active, the siblings elect one by its fixed rule, and a lone session is elected alone (owner rulings, 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-13). Do not assume none. A stale memory of “there was one yesterday” is not an answer in either direction. “The owner said merge” is still required. Submitting to main is the owner’s call (§”Ask the user before submitting”), and this does not change that. The eight checks, each named in a refusal by number and id: . | base — open, based on main, and the base is not the head branch of a merged PR. A stacked PR is retargeted by its owning session first. | ready-for-review — not a draft, and the latest ready_for_review event is attributable to the PR’s own session, never to yours. When the merge manager lands a PR of its own, --no-merge-manager lifts the “never to yours” half (§”When no Merge Manager is active”). | ready-marker — a ready: <sha> comment signed with the PR’s own session link (the one in its body), naming the head, or with only merge-main bot merges after it. | labels — ready-to-merge present, needs-merge-human absent. | ci — gates a release only (--release, or the release label; owner, card Q-CIB-4 A, 2026-11-08). On any other merge the judgement below is made and reported, and the check passes as advisory. The judgement: every pull_request run on the head is success or skipped, and every workflow owed for that event ran. A workflow_dispatch run counts only as the stand-in for a pull_request run GitHub held for approval (action_required) on a head that is a merge-main bot merge: merge-main has already merged main into that head, so the head IS the merge, and a dispatch on it judges the tree that would land. The latest dispatch of the same workflow on the head decides — green counts, running is not-ready, red is a defect. Held with no dispatch: not-ready if merge-main.yml’s for wf in … ; do gh workflow run line names that workflow’s file (the dispatch is still owed), reported not judged if it does not (Feature Staging, preview-only), and unknown if that line cannot be parsed. A green dispatch never rescues a pull_request run that executed and went red, and anywhere else it is reported and not counted. Feature Staging is judged, never waited for: a staging run still in flight, or not started, is not a refusal — its deploy is held by the gh-pages rate limit — and the verdict says so as not waited for. Once it finishes, red still refuses, since stage runs real checks before it deploys — unless the only failed step is the deploy itself (DEPLOY_ONLY_STEP): a push window that never opened, or three rejected pushes, is not a verdict on the tree. The guard reads the run’s failed steps to tell; if it cannot read them, red refuses as before. The list is NOT_WAITED_FOR_WORKFLOW_FILES in merge-guard.ts. | checklist — no unticked - [ ] in the body. | open-question — no comment after the marker asks the owner or the Merge Manager a question (a heuristic; its limits are on openQuestions in the script — a fresh ready: after the answer moves the window). | mergeable — GitHub says the head still merges cleanly into main Check 5’s runs tested the head merged with main as main was when the head was pushed; once main moves, a stale green head with a valid marker can pass checks 1-7 while it conflicts. The PR API’s mergeable: false (mergeable_state: dirty) refuses not-ready — merge main into the head and re-sign ready:. mergeable: null means GitHub has not computed it yet: the guard re-asks for up to 14 s, then reports unknown, never a pass. unstable and blocked pass here, because they are about checks and reviews, which check 5 and the owner judge. A verdict is a snapshot and can go stale on exactly this check when main moves; --merge re-evaluates live. | . Exit 0 is pass (or merged), 1 refused, 2 could not determine — never a pass. A refusal is handed back to the owning session through merge-refusal.bpmn with the check’s text; the steward does not fix the PR to make it pass. What the OWNING session does, so a finished PR passes: mark it ready, then post ready: <head sha> signed with its session link — https://claude.ai/code/session_… in the footer — within ten minutes of each other, and apply ready-to-merge. Every session acts with the owner’s token, so the timeline’s actor is always the owner and cannot tell sessions apart; the signature is the only thing that can. An unsigned marker is refused. A verdict has four states, and red means wrong, not unfinished. A PR that is merely not ready yet (a draft, no marker, no label, an unticked box, CI still running, an open question, a conflict with main) is pending. Only a defect is failure: a base that is not main or is dead, needs-merge-human, red CI on the head, or a marker or ready-flip by a session other than the PR’s own. success is pass and error is could-not-determine. Red on every draft would teach readers to ignore red. Only success lands. No workflow runs it. The guard is the script alone, and --merge evaluates live at the moment it lands. Rule_NotReady in merge-priority.dmn applies the cheap half of checks 1-3 at placement (readiness, from LivePr.draft, baseRef, readySha, readyBy), so an unfinished PR is handed back before it is put in a train rather than at the PUT.

6901.title: When the authors stall: the steward dispatches unblockers
6901.content: Authors’ sessions can hit usage limits together, so the whole hand-back column can go quiet while every member in it is one small fix away from admission. The steward may dispatch agents for small unblocking fixes, without using up the CI budget. This adds a second actor to step 4 above. It changes nothing else. An unblocker fixes the head. It never merges, never adds ready-to-merge, and never posts a ready: marker. The author still vouches for the PR, and the steward still lands it only after the author signals ready, or under the owner’s explicit release. Who goes: the PRs merge:steward routes to hand-back. Leave out drafts, PRs whose author was active in the last 15 minutes, PRs another session has claimed, and PRs under an owner block (a ruling such as “this blocks the PR” is a judgement about content, and fixing the code does not lift it). Group them into a few agents, each in its own worktree. The general swarm rules are in swarm-management. Every unblocker gets the same rules, written once and handed to all of them: . | rule | why | . | at most ONE push per PR, after bun run cat gates locally — or, when every conflict was generated, after the targeted checks of merge-conflict-patterns §”A merge round — run each check ONCE” | each push runs full CI and deploys a staging preview into gh-pages, which has a size budget. Pushing speculatively spends both | . | no workflow_dispatch, re-run, empty commit or close/reopen | the same budget, and a dispatched run is not an owed run (above) | . | the merge manager re-runs only a PR it is about to merge, never held content, never in a batch, never during a GitHub outage, and refreshes a re-pin PR’s pins first (merge-manager-watcher §”Re-run policy”) | every failed run emails the owner; re-runs were most of the 11-11 failure emails (card Q-RERUN-1 B) | . | merge commits only: no rebase, amend or force-push | it is somebody else’s branch | . | authored conflict → resolve only dead code, or a pure addition carried over verbatim; otherwise quote both sides and stand down | choosing between two behaviours is the author’s call | . | git submodule update --init and bun run cat state:mount before regen | without the submodules merge:steward cannot load. Without the mount, fsh-guts:viz:check exits non-zero (it judges that the mounted graph renders; the page itself is built at publish) and audit:coverage:strict goes red | . | delete the worktree’s node_modules at the end | four parallel installs run out of the container’s disk | . | one comment per PR: root cause, the commit it pushed or the reason it stood down | the author comes back to an explanation, not a mystery commit | . missing-required is often a head that CI never started, not a slow one. The causes to check, in order: . | the PR edits a workflow file and GitHub cannot parse it, so no run is created at all; | the head was pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, which starts no pull_request run; | the run is held at action_required. | . The first one is not visible in the check list, so look at the YAML. After any merge of main, check for silently dropped files. Some files under */test/results/ (LSI indexes, QA and detangle sidecars) are gitignored but still tracked. Once a resolution step removes one from the index, regen rewrites it on disk and git add -A does not stage it again. Local checks still pass, but CI’s fresh checkout fails. merge:main and the merge-main bot refuse such a merge and name the paths (droppedInMerge in merge-base.ts, see merge-conflict-patterns §”When one side deleted the file”). A hand git merge gets no such check. After one, run git diff --diff-filter=D HEAD^1 HEAD -- '*/test/results/*', and restore anything that main still tracks with git checkout HEAD^2 -- <path>. Stalled for days, with no handover report: write it, then hand it to a takeover agent . An unblocker suits a short pause. When the authors are gone for days, the steward does something else: . | Writes the handover report each author did not. It goes as one comment per PR, headed ## Takeover plan, in the handover-report format and measured, not recalled: intent with the owner’s rulings quoted; head SHA, conflicts split into authored and generated, owed CI; done and remaining; approval and any scope drift; ordered next steps with their falsifiers; owner questions; couplings with other open PRs. This step is read-only apart from the comment. | Gives the owner one paste-able brief for the takeover agent: the cold start, the work order across PRs (the couplings decide it), the merge rules, and the open owner questions. The owner starts that agent, possibly on another account, so the brief must stand alone. | The takeover session becomes each PR’s owning session. merge:guard accepts a ready: marker only from the session the PR body names, and check 2 keeps the merging session from vouching for its own landing. So the takeover agent edits the body’s session line to its own session, records “taken over from . (stalled)", claims the work items, and then signs. The steward never signs for it, and there is no one-time bypass. | . A PR that is green but refused by checks 3 and 4 (no marker, no label) is waiting-on-author in the queue, not active, until the takeover session signs it.

6902.title: Landing
6902.content: Re-run merge:steward after every merge, before the next one. Each merge moves main. A member admitted against the old main can turn dirty and then cannot land at all: its tested head is still green, but GitHub refuses to merge a conflicted PR, so it waits for its merge:main round and fresh CI on the new head. Only with the owner’s release, which is the authorisation half of merge-to-main (Call_MergeToMain in merge-train.bpmn): explicit, or a standing ruling quoted verbatim with its date, and only through bun run cat merge:guard <pr> --merge --session <id> (section above). What lands is exactly the SHA CI tested — the guard pins the PUT to the head it evaluated, so GitHub refuses it if the head moved; if main moved after the train’s CI started, re-run rather than land. A standing release covers the queue AS IT STOOD, not every PR that arrives later. New PRs need the owner’s explicit approval. So on every sweep the steward lists the PRs opened since the release, and puts them to the owner in one question, with the table’s verdict on each. One answer (“approve all 6”) may cover the whole batch.

6903.title: Post-merge asymmetry: why main needs its own regeneration pipeline
6903.content: .github/workflows/merge-main.yml runs bun run cat merge:main on an opted-in PR branch when main moves, resolving declared conflicts and regenerating. There is a structural asymmetry in the other direction: after a PR merges into main, nothing in that workflow regenerates main. So any merge changing an enumerated or counted directory can leave main red on a hard gate, even when the PR merged cleanly with zero git conflicts. The only reason it usually does not is an accident: the PR branch happened to regenerate against a base that had not moved yet. When that accident does not hold, main goes red and stays red until somebody notices. The accidental-repair pattern . A PR that adds files without regenerating a counted README breaks main; a later, unrelated PR whose branch carries a regenerated README repairs it incidentally; a web-UI upload breaks it again with no generator run at all. The trap: A green on a derived gate must NOT be read as “was never broken” or “the commit before it was clean”. Unrelated PR branches that happen to carry regenerated files incidentally repair main, creating untrustworthy gate histories. Why this halts development: While main is red on a hard gate, every open PR inherits that red, so no PR can show green, and nothing can be merged on green CI. PR sessions start debugging their own diffs for failures that belong to main. Where derived artefacts are regenerated . No automation pushes to main and none opens a repair PR: the automation/post-merge-regen-<sha> branches and their PRs piled up with no CI once Actions could no longer open PRs here, and they are gone. A full regen composes and regenerates the whole index, 50-80 minutes of runner time, so it runs only when a person dispatches it or the release build calls it. No pull request, push or schedule event starts one. | For a PR, by hand, before it merges. Dispatch post-merge-regen.yml with pr set to the PR’s number or branch (gh workflow run post-merge-regen.yml -f pr=<n>). It runs the regen writers at the PR’s head. When a tracked file changed, it commits ONE chore(derived): regenerate derived artefacts for <sha> to the PR’s own branch; for a fork’s PR it commits nothing and fails with the command to run. The PR’s checks judge that commit, so the regen reaches main through the normal, tested merge. Pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, the commit starts no CI and the run fails saying so; a REGEN_PUSH_TOKEN secret lets the checks start by themselves. A head that is itself a regen commit and still regenerates fails (no fixpoint), so it cannot loop. | At release, automatically. release-npm.yml regenerates into the package it publishes (a patch applied to the release checkout, never committed) and publishes nothing when a check is unrepaired. | On main, by hand: verify and warn. post-merge-regen.yml with pr empty regenerates in its runner, warns with what was stale, and commits, pushes and opens nothing. NEGATIVE CONTROL: a main with nothing stale warns about nothing. | . Branch and staging preview builds do not regenerate. Merge steward procedure: post-merge verification . | A PR carries its own regen. When a PR changes the inputs of a derived file, its author (or the steward) dispatches the regen for it before it merges. The PR’s own gates report a stale derived file as they always did. | Main stale on a derived gate: dispatch the verify run to see what is stale, then dispatch the regen for the next PR in the queue, or for a PR opened only to carry it, which is admitted with priority under merge-priority.dmn as an unblock-main repair. | A red regen run is that PR’s failure, like any other check: a fork PR runs the regen it names, and a regen commit pushed without CI needs one more push before the PR’s checks run. | .

6904.title: ACK every PR that enters the queue, on its bean (STRICT)
6904.content: A submitter who hears nothing cannot tell “queued” from “lost”, and the work item is where the next session looks. When a PR enters the queue (first seen on a sweep, or approved by the owner), the steward writes three things in the same change: . | The queue entry, beans/queue/<owner>--<repo>--<pr>.json. It holds the table’s placement, a reason that begins ACK: and says what the PR waits on, and beans, copied from the PR body. Validate it against MergeQueueEntrySchema. | A note on each work item the PR serves, one file per work item per branch: beans/notes/<bean>--<date>--<branch>.md. A note, never an append to the work item def; bean-coordination (opt-in cat-harness.work-plan) says why. Then run bun run cat beans:notes, or CI’s beans:notes:check goes red. | One comment on the PR naming the entry and the work items. Before the work items cutover, items 1 and 2 reach main only through the steward’s own PR, a cycle late, so the comment is the ACK the author sees now. After the cutover, write 1 and 2 with state:push; the comment then just points at them. | . A PR whose body names no work item gets the entry with beans: [] and a comment asking the author to name one. The steward does not invent the association.

6905.title: Every open PR has an entry: review the whole list, then triage it
6905.content: merge:steward skips drafts, and a PR that nobody ACKed has no entry, so the queue silently shrinks to the PRs someone happened to look at. On a review, and at least once per working session: . | List every open PR, drafts included, from the API; not from the steward’s table and not from memory. | Every PR without an entry gets one with status: "unknown". A draft gets the placement rule: "draft", class: "hand-back", rank: 99, and its decision names the steward, not the DMN, because the table never placed it. Claiming the table did would be a fact the steward invented. | Triage each one into a status (QUEUE_STATUSES in schemas/sdlc/merge-queue.ts), with the evidence in reason: . | status | when | . | active | its author pushed or commented within 24 hours | . | waiting-on-author | handed back with a named ask, and the author is not back yet | . | blocked | waits on another PR, work item or ruling, named in reason | . | stale | no push and no human comment for more than 24 hours. Bot pushes from merge-main do not count as activity | . | approval-void | the owner approved it, and then its scope changed | . | landed | merged. The entry stays as history; it is never deleted | . | Report the stale ones to the owner as a decision, never close them: closing a PR is the author’s or the owner’s call (deletion-requires-confirmation). | . An approval is for the content that was approved. A branch can change scope after approval. Compare the title and the changed-file count against what was approved before landing. On a mismatch, set approval-void and ask again.

6906.title: Your merge cadence is an input to the bot’s throughput
6906.content: Pacing and concurrency are one question, not two. merge-main.yml sweeps the merge-main-labelled PRs on every push to main, so each merge you land starts a sweep — and the per-PR merge job’s concurrency group decides what happens to the sweep already running. A sweep takes 1–15 minutes, and a steward draining the queue can land a merge more often than that. cancel-in-progress is trigger-dependent, so a push sweep QUEUES behind the running one rather than killing it. The rule: . | A sweep in flight is work in progress — do not count a PR as unmergeable while its merge job is queued behind your last landing. Re-read it after the sweep settles. | When you are landing faster than the sweep completes, you are the reason the behind-PRs are not catching up. A merge still carries only main@T(n-1) -> T(n) per sweep; a burst of landings leaves a backlog of steps to carry. | .

6907.title: A hold has an EXPIRY and a trigger, or it outlives its reason
6907.content: A hold is a decision, and like every queue entry it records what the steward decided — not a fact. Facts move. So a hold is only valid while the condition that justified it is still true, and the steward re-derives that condition at every sweep rather than inheriting it. Write a hold with three parts or do not write one: . | part | why | . | what it waits on | the condition, stated so it can be checked mechanically | . | what ends it | the observation that lifts it, not a time | . | what it costs | which PRs are being held, so the price is visible | . Two failures that both look like diligence: . | Inheriting a hold across its own justification. Once the condition a hold waited on has passed, the hold must go. A hold whose reason you cannot restate from current facts is not a hold, it is a habit. | Holding to protect a PR that was already conflicted. A head that needs a forward merge whatever happens is protected by nothing. If the thing you are protecting already needs the work your hold is avoiding, the hold is free of benefit and not free of cost. | .

6908.title: Sweep the whole queue; a tracked handful is not the queue
6908.content: Compute the mergeable set from the open-PR list every time, never from the PRs you happen to be following. A PR not in your mental list is in no list at all. The sweep is cheap and mechanical: for every open non-draft PR, read base.ref, run git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head> for the rc, and read the check runs on that exact head. Three columns, one pass. A PR with base == main and rc == 0 is a candidate; whether it is mergeable is still the OWED question above, not a count of failures. no failures and nothing pending is NOT green. One completed check out of the full suite reads bad=0 wait=0 because almost nothing has been asked: a gate that did not fire is indistinguishable from one that passed, and a tally of failures cannot tell them apart. So the third column is the owed SET, never a count: compare the check-run names on that head against the set owed for its event, and treat a missing name exactly as a red one. A steward that cannot say why it is not merging a PR which is green on the owed set is holding it by accident; one that merges on bad=0 wait=0 alone is merging unverified. The exact meaning of “all green” for a merge, including the full tier and superseded cancelled jobs, is rule 1 of merge-manager-watcher §”Merge-sweep rules”. bun run cat merge:watch prints that verdict for every open PR.

6909.title: Read base.ref BEFORE anything else: a stacked PR is not a main-queue member
6909.content: merge-tree origin/main <head> answers a question nobody asked when the PR’s base is not main. Mergeability, independence and placement are all computed against the base, so a stacked PR measured against main is measured against the wrong tree — and the merge button lands it on the wrong tree too. A PR merged onto a stacked base closes as merged while its commits are not on main. The tell is cheap and it is first: gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n> --jq .base.ref. A queue sweep must print the base. A stacked PR is not admitted to the main queue. Either its base lands first and the PR is re-measured against main, or it is rebased onto main by its author. The steward’s job is to notice, not to resolve it. GitHub does not retarget a stacked PR when its base PR merges. It retargets only when the base BRANCH is deleted, and these repositories keep merged branches. So “stacked on #N, GitHub retargets to main when #N merges”, a sentence a PR body may well carry, is false here. Read base.ref again after the lower PR merges, and retarget it yourself (PATCH .../pulls/<n> with base=main) before merging.

6910.title: git add -A after a merge silently reverts the submodule gitlinks
6910.content: And git submodule status does not catch it. A merge resolves a submodule gitlink like any other path. git add -A then re-records every submodule at whatever the working tree happens to have checked out, overwriting the resolution. If you initialised submodules before merging, and the base advanced them, you have just reverted them to the merge base — and git submodule status shows no + and no -, because the index and the working tree agree with each other. They are simply both wrong. The symptom is usually not a submodule error but regen reporting checks as “a real defect, not staleness”, from a module-load failure such as an export not found in a submodule script. Two rules follow: . | Stage explicitly after a merge, never git add -A, while any submodule is in the tree. | Verify the pins against the ref, not against the working tree. git ls-tree <ref> bootstrap bootstrap-tools is what exposes this; git submodule status cannot, and a check that cannot see the defect is not evidence of its absence. | .

6911.title: A local gate run in a contended container is not evidence — and here is the ratio
6911.content: A bun test shard in a shared agent container can run about ten times slower than on a dedicated runner, and at that ratio the default 5 s per-test budget stops measuring the code: . grep -c "timed out after 5000ms" -> N grep -cE "^error:|Expected:|Received:|toBe|toEqual" -> 0 . So the signature is cheap to check and worth checking before you believe a red local run: all failures are timed out after Nms and the assertion-failure count is zero. That is contention. Report it as inconclusive under contention — never as green, and never as a defect — and let CI on the exact sha be the authority. What you must not do is “fix” a test that is not broken, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green applies with full force here, because the temptation is strongest when the failure is not real. Two ways to get this measurement wrong: . | A count read from a partial log, before the run ends, is not a count. | A compound command’s exit status is the last command’s, and a test runner’s status has to be captured before anything else runs. | .

6912.title: Agentic pre-merge review: warn-only and the would-have-blocked counterfactual
6912.content: Agentic merge review is warn-only. Architectural decision: staying WARN-ONLY with measured justification . The decision to keep agentic code review warn-only is governed by empirical evidence, not caution: . | Literature gap: Across five ingested agentic SE papers (CodeAgent arXiv:2402.02172v5, SWE-Debate arXiv:2404.04834v4, SWE-Router arXiv:2507.23348v1, TCAndon-Router arXiv:2601.04544v1, He et al. arXiv:2607.00053v1), zero empirical false-positive rates (FPR) exist for an LLM judge. | CodeAgent’s unconfirmed flag rate: CodeAgent’s own human annotation revealed that 48.6% of GPT-4’s flags were unconfirmed. A reviewer where nearly half of all flags are unconfirmed cannot be a blocking gate. | SWE-Router & SWE-Debate noise boundaries: LLM-as-a-judge suffers from self-enhancement bias, verbosity bias, and positional bias. | Deterministic compile checks stay blocking: G5 (Lean module compilation), G6 (SUSHI FHIR compilation), and G7 (JSON-LD schema validation) are deterministic compile gates that have exact binary outcomes and remain blocking. An agentic reviewer does not share this property. | Backlog inversion: A blocking gate over an active codebase with unreviewed content nodes would fail on existing background patterns rather than PR delta, inverting the order of necessary backfill. | . The counterfactual instrument: why only a warn-only phase can measure FPR . A blocking gate destroys the counterfactual: when a gate blocks, authors modify code, bypass checks, or abandon PRs. It is impossible to determine whether the flagged condition would have actually broken production or represented a false positive. By contrast, a warn-only gate records blocking-severity findings as “would have blocked” (WouldHaveBlockedRecordSchema in schemas/sdlc/merge-queue.ts), pinned to the PR’s headSha. The PR then merges to main. Subsequent monitoring observes whether any defect materialized, enabling humans to adjudicate findings: . | true_positive: Finding correctly identified a genuine defect. | false_positive: Finding flagged benign, correct code. | unknown: Third state (inconclusive, unverified, or cannot be determined). | . The third-state rule: unknown is strictly preserved and never folded into true_positive (which would artificially deflate FPR) or false_positive (which would artificially inflate FPR). Pre-registered promotion criteria . To prevent choosing thresholds to fit data, promotion criteria are registered as numbers and windows before data collection begins (AgenticPromotionCriteriaSchema): . | minimumPrWindow: 50 evaluated PRs. | maximumFalsePositiveRate: <= 0.05 (5% FPR: confirmedFalsePositives / (confirmedTruePositives + confirmedFalsePositives)). | minimumReviewCoverage: >= 0.80 (80% non-unknown adjudication: (confirmedTruePositives + confirmedFalsePositives) / warnedFindings). | . Until all three criteria are empirically proven, the agentic review remains warn-only.

6913.title: Tool-integrated agentic pre-merge review (CodeAgent / 2402.02172v5)
6913.content: Codified in research/methodologies/agentic-pre-merge-review.md (opt-in cat-harness.research). Multi-agent tool-integrated code review architectures (Tang et al., arXiv:2402.02172v5) structure automated pre-merge evaluation into specialized roles (Reviewer, Coder, QA-Checker, Consistency, Security) across four sequential phases. Three operational rules govern its integration into this repository’s merge queue: . | The Deterministic vs. Judged Boundary: Deterministic compile gates (Lean formal proofs, SUSHI/FHIR IG AST, JSON-LD schema renders, linter and test suites) answer questions with one computable truth — these MUST BLOCK. LLM-mediated agentic code reviews answer questions with uncalibrated error rates — these MUST WARN (“would have blocked”), exiting 0 and logging structured finding sidecars. | The False-Positive Guard: an automated review gate must never block merge on unverified LLM assertions (see the unconfirmed flag rate above). Promotion from warn to block requires measured calibration against recorded repository defects, per the pre-registered criteria above. | Bounded Dialogue Budgets: Conversational QA-Checker loops must cap at a maximum of 2 adjustment iterations to avoid latency explosions (CodeAgent measured 5 min / $0.122 per review) and context window exhaustion. Deterministic formatters and linters must run directly in CLI gates (bun run cat gates) rather than consuming multi-turn LLM reasoning. | .

6922.doc: Merge request: find or elect the merge manager
6922.title: Merge request: find or elect the merge manager
6922.content: Process_MergeRequest · strict (defaulted) · 8 step(s) . The sibling’s side of merging. A coding agent whose work depends on an unmerged PR stacks on it rather than waiting, and retargets when it lands. With a PR ready to merge it does not know whether a merge manager exists, so it checks: if one is active and live, it sends the six-line merge request; if none is, it elects one with its siblings by the fixed rule (a lone session is elected alone), the winner announcing itself to all and taking the lane. Only the merge manager merges and re-pins (owner rulings, 2026-11-13): no other session merges, and a PR green except for a re-pin is sent as repin+merge. Any agent may stall, the merge manager included: a request not acknowledged within the stall window sends the sibling to stalled-agent triage and a re-election without the stalled session. The merge manager’s own loop is Process_MergeManagerWatch. Source: owner rulings, 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-13. Ready to merge is defined in merge-queue §”What ‘ready to merge’ means”; a ready PR merges at once, lowest dependency first, and a lower repository never waits on a higher one (owner, 2026-11-15). i i i i i i i i

6924.title: Lanes — who acts
6924.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Sibling session | sibling-session | Any coding agent with a PR ready to merge. It first checks whether a merge manager is active; if none is and one is needed, it elects one with its siblings by the fixed rule; a lone or lapsed session manages its own PRs. It never merges another session’s PR, never pushes to another session’s branch, and treats a merge manager that does not acknowledge within the stall window as stalled. It never waits for a dependency to merge: it stacks on the dependency PR and keeps working. | .

6925.doc: Merge request: find or elect the merge manager
6925.title: Steps
6925.content: Every one of the 8 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Elect the merge manager with the siblingsSib_Elect | Sibling session | merge-manager-watcher | The deterministic rule (electHolder): the active session that owns the P0 PR, else the earliest-created active session, the session id breaking a tie. Stalled sessions are not candidates. Every sibling computes the same answer from the same listing (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). | . | Announce and note the merge managerSib_Announce | Sibling session | merge-manager-watcher | Send “merge manager: <session id>” to every sibling and the owner, and note it durably on the coordination work item, so it is used by all, including siblings started later. | . | Send the six-line merge requestSib_Send | Sibling session | merge-manager-watcher | To the merge manager: the PR URL and full head SHA, the session URL, 1-3 sentences on the change, the rendered preview URL or no preview with a reason, what to look for, and full tier green as judged (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). Never merge it yourself, and never push to another session’s branch. A PR green except for a re-pin is sent as repin+merge: <owner/repo>#<n> <sha> with the same six lines; never re-pin it yourself, and never merge (owner ruling, 2026-11-13). | . | Stalled-agent triageSib_CallStalled | Sibling session | calls Stalled-agent triage: collect handovers, consolidate themes, recommend, re-route | Tell the owner that the merge manager stalled, then re-elect with the stalled session excluded. The new holder announces itself, takes over the queue and tells the owner. | . | Merge manager watchSib_CallWatch | Sibling session | calls Merge manager watch: wake, read the queue live, route | The elected session holds the merge steward lane and runs its loop until it hands over or the lane lapses. | . | Stack on it and keep workingSib_Stack | Sibling session | continual-progress | Same repository: branch from the dependency PR’s branch and open a draft PR whose base is that branch; pull the dependency in with merge commits, never rebase or force-push another session’s branch. Across layers: develop against the dependency’s branch laid over a fresh mount; a draft may pin the dependency PR’s full head SHA, never a branch. Write “stacked on <repo>#<n>” in the PR body. A re-pin is its own PR holding only pins; work that needs the new pins stacks on it, and a fix the re-pin needs lands in its owning layer (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). | . | When the base lands, retargetSib_Retarget | Sibling session | continual-progress | Retarget the PR onto main and merge main in; across layers, send repin+merge: the merge manager re-pins to the dependency’s merge commit on main, so pins only move forward (owner ruling, 2026-11-13). Never merge the stacked PR into its base branch, and never mark it ready while it pins an unmerged commit. | . | Make the PR readySib_Ready | Sibling session | continual-progress | Its own work is done and its full tier is green as judged; it is marked ready by the queue rule (continual-progress, Pace the ready marking). | .
